### CR-M049 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.Hardware
- **Title:** ReadData buffer accessed from DataReceived thread without synchronization
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.Hardware\Ports/Serial.cs:54,58,121-132,144`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — every ReadData access (Read/HasReadData/RemoveReadData/Clear/ReadSerial) is now serialized on a dedicated _readLock (was only ReadSerial, on the SerialPort instance); RemoveReadData copies-and-removes atomically (also fixing the -1 RemoveRange crash). ### CR-M052 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.Modbus
- **Title:** TCP response transaction ID is parsed but never validated against the request
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.Modbus\Protocols/ModbusClient.cs:165-174, Protocols/ModbusFrame.cs:28`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — the MBAP transaction id is threaded into WaitAndParseResponse for TCP and validated against the response; a mismatch throws IOException instead of accepting a stale/out-of-order frame. Regression test crafts a wrong-txId response and asserts the throw.
- **Detail:** SendReadRequest/SendWriteRequest generate a per-request txId and ParseTcpResponse extracts the response transaction ID, but nothing compares the two. A stale or out-of-order response (e.g. left over after a prior timeout, despite the _port.Clear() before each request) would be accepted as the answer to the current request. The MBAP transaction ID exists precisely to correlate request/response; discarding it removes the protocol's safety check.
- **Fix:** Pass the sent txId into WaitAndParseResponse for TCP and throw (or keep reading) when response.TransactionId != txId.

### CR-M053 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.Network
- **Title:** TOCTOU between Read and RemoveRange in RemoveReadData can remove more bytes than were returned
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.Network\Ports/TcpIp.cs:146-154 (same in Ports/Udp.cs:136-144)`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — not reproducible: RemoveReadData in both TcpIp and Udp already performs the copy-and-remove atomically inside a single lock(ReadData), removing exactly result.Length (fixed with CR-H026/H027).
- **Detail:** RemoveReadData calls Read(size) to copy out bytes, re-checks HasReadData(size), then RemoveRange(0, size) — three separate unsynchronized operations over a buffer the worker thread is concurrently appending to. Even ignoring the append race, the returned `result` and the removed range are computed at different instants; combined with the missing lock this is a classic time-of-check/time-of-use hazard. Should be a single atomic copy-and-remove.
- **Fix:** Inside one `lock (ReadData)`: compute count = size < 0 ? ReadData.Count : Math.Min(size, ReadData.Count); take GetRange(0, count).ToArray(); RemoveRange(0, count); return.

### CR-M054 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.Network
- **Title:** Udp.Write passes possibly-null _remoteEndPoint (CS8604 nullable warning)
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.Network\Ports/Udp.cs:34-43`
- **Category:** nullable · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — Udp.Write now guards _remoteEndPoint alongside _client before calling UdpClient.Send, removing the CS8604 nullable warning and the latent NRE.

UdpClient.Send's endpoint parameter is non-nullable, so this is a CS8604 dereference-of-possibly-null warning, which the framework's 'No nullable warnings' convention forbids. _remoteEndPoint is only assigned in Open(); if a derived/edge path leaves _client non-null but _remoteEndPoint null the send also fails at runtime.
- **Fix:** Guard `_remoteEndPoint` alongside `_client` (or after Open()) before calling Send, e.g. `if (_client != null && _remoteEndPoint != null) _client.Send(...);`.

### CR-M056 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.NFC
- **Title:** Polling loops swallow all exceptions / fire-and-forget Task.Run with no error surface
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.NFC\Transports/SerialNfcTransport.cs:110`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — added an INfcTransport.PollingError event; SerialNfcTransport/HttpNfcTransport/HidNfcTransport now wrap the poll loop in try/catch (surfacing non-cancellation faults via PollingError and stopping), track the poll Task, and StopPollingAsync awaits it. Http keeps HttpRequestException transient but surfaces JsonException/other faults. Regression tests drive a malformed-body and a thrown fault and assert PollingError fires.
- **Detail:** StartPollingAsync launches `_ = Task.Run(async () => { while(...) { ReadTagAsync(...); Task.Delay(...); } })` with no try/catch around the body. SerialNfcTransport.ReadTagAsync calls _port.Read/_port.Write which throw on serial errors (port unplugged, TimeoutException from the 2000ms ReadTimeout inside Task.Run, InvalidOperationException if the port closes mid-poll). Any such throw faults the detached task silently: polling stops with no event, no log, and IsConnected may still read true. HttpNfcTransport only catches HttpRequestException, so a JSON deserialization error (JsonException) or non-success status from EnsureSuccessStatusCode likewise kills the loop silently. The detached task is also not awaited or tracked, so StopPollingAsync cancels the token but cannot observe completion.
- **Fix:** Wrap the loop body in try/catch, surface failures via an event or by re-checking cancellation, and store the polling Task so StopPollingAsync can await its completion.

### CR-M060 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.REST
- **Title:** Sync wrappers block on async via GetAwaiter().GetResult()
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.REST\RestClient.cs:99-104,127-132,156-161,184-189,212-217`

### CR-M064 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SOAP

### CR-M065 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SOAP
- **Title:** SoapServer.Dispose does sync-over-async on StopAsync (deadlock risk)

- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — extracted a synchronous Stop() core (Cancel/Stop/Close/Dispose are all sync); Dispose calls Stop() directly instead of blocking on StopAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(); StopAsync is now a thin wrapper (removed the noise await Task.CompletedTask). Regression test: Stop/Dispose/StopAsync on an unstarted server don't throw or hang.
- **Detail:** Dispose calls StopAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult(). StopAsync itself is fake-async (it does synchronous work then awaits Task.CompletedTask at line 93), so today it happens to complete synchronously, but the sync-over-async pattern is fragile: if StopAsync ever gains real async work, blocking on it from Dispose can deadlock in contexts with a synchronization context. StopAsync's trailing 'await Task.CompletedTask' is also pure noise.
- **Fix:** Make Stop synchronous (Cancel/Stop/Close/Dispose are all sync APIs) and have Dispose call the synchronous core directly; keep an async StopAsync wrapper if needed for the public surface, but do not block on it in Dispose.

The 'clean old entries' step prunes timestamps within an existing key's list but never removes a key whose list has become empty. Every caller passes a meaningful message — SseAuthenticationMiddleware.cs:40 forwards result.ErrorMessage, SseCorsMiddleware.cs:56 passes 'Origin not allowed', SseRateLimitMiddleware.cs:68 passes 'Too many connection attempts' — and all of them are dropped on the floor, so denial responses carry only a status code with no diagnostic text.

### CR-M069 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SSE
- **Title:** Query-string token extraction breaks on leading '?' and value-embedded '='
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.SSE\Middleware/SseAuthenticationService.cs:160-173`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — ExtractTokenFromQueryString now TrimStart('?')s the query and splits each pair with Split('=', 2), so a raw query with a leading ? and a token value containing = (e.g. base64 padding) are handled instead of causing spurious 401s. Regression test covers both.
- **Detail:** ExtractTokenFromQueryString splits on '&' then on '='. Two problems: (1) if queryString includes the leading '?' (common when callers pass the raw query), the first pair key becomes '?token' and never matches QueryTokenName, so the token is missed; (2) parts.Length == 2 rejects any value containing an '=' (e.g. base64 JWTs ending in '=' padding, or '=' inside the token), so valid tokens fail auth. Both cause spurious 401s.
- **Fix:** TrimStart('?') the query string first, and split each pair with `pair.Split('=', 2)` (limit 2) then check parts.Length >= 2, joining/taking the remainder as the value before UnescapeDataString.

### CR-M070 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SSE
- **Title:** SseClient.ConnectAsync leaks the previous CTS and receive task on repeated calls
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.SSE\SseClient.cs:94-103`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — ConnectAsync tears down any prior session (via DisconnectAsync) before creating a new CTS/receive task, so repeated calls no longer orphan the previous CancellationTokenSource and ReceiveLoop. Covered by a bounded double-connect test.
- **Detail:** ConnectAsync unconditionally overwrites _cts (and _receiveTask) without cancelling/disposing any prior instance. Calling ConnectAsync twice (or reconnect logic) abandons the first CancellationTokenSource — undisposed IDisposable — and orphans the first ReceiveLoop task, which keeps running. There is no guard against an already-connected state.

### CR-M071 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SSE
- **Title:** Client receive pipeline is an unimplemented stub — ProcessEventLine and event callbacks are never reached
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.SSE\SseClient.cs:133-156`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — SseClient now performs real HTTP SSE streaming: ConnectAsync opens a GET with ResponseHeadersRead (injectable HttpClient), ReceiveLoop reads lines and feeds ProcessEventLine (so OnMessage/OnEvent/LastEventId/retry actually fire), with AutoReconnect re-opening via Last-Event-ID. Test streams events through a mock handler and asserts the callbacks; a 404 makes ConnectAsync throw.
- **Detail:** ReceiveLoop does no network I/O — it just `await Task.Delay(100)` in a loop until cancelled. Consequently ProcessEventLine (SseClient.cs:161) is never invoked by the client, so _currentEvent, OnMessage, OnEvent, LastEventId-from-stream, and the retry/reconnect handling are all dead in practice. ConnectAsync also reports IsConnected=true and fires OnConnected without ever opening a connection, so the client's public contract (connect, receive events, auto-reconnect) is not actually fulfilled. This reads as scaffolding rather than a working client.
- **Fix:** Implement the HTTP streaming read (HttpClient with ResponseHeadersRead, read lines, feed ProcessEventLine) or clearly mark the type abstract/partial so consumers must supply the transport, mirroring how SseClientConnection.OnSendAsync is a documented override point on the server side.

### CR-M072 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.SSE
- **Title:** SseEvent.CreateComment produces a malformed comment line
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.SSE\SseEvent.cs:105-111`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — comments are represented by a distinct SseEvent.Comment property serialized as ": {comment}" lines; CreateComment sets Comment (not Data), so ToString emits a real SSE comment instead of "data: : comment". The existing test was corrected to assert the fixed output.
- **Detail:** CreateComment sets Data = ": comment". ToString() then emits each Data line prefixed with 'data: ', producing `data: : comment` — a data field, not an SSE comment. A real SSE comment line must literally start with ':' with no 'data:' prefix. The current output is a normal (mis-prefixed) data event, defeating the documented keep-alive purpose and corrupting the event stream.
- **Fix:** Represent comments distinctly (e.g. a Comment property serialized as `: {comment}` lines) rather than smuggling them through Data, or special-case Data values beginning with ':' in ToString().

### CR-M073 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Communication.WebSocket
- **Title:** Synchronous .Wait() on WebSocket async I/O (sync-over-async)
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Communication.WebSocket\Ports/WebSocketPort.cs:44,85,114,136`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — WebSocketPort Write/Open/Close/ReadWorker now block via ConfigureAwait(false).GetAwaiter().GetResult() instead of .Wait()/.Result, so the original WebSocketException propagates (not an AggregateException) and no captured SynchronizationContext is required.
- **Detail:** Write/Open/Close/ReadWorker block on async WebSocket operations via .Wait()/.Result (SendAsync().Wait(), ConnectAsync().Wait(), CloseAsync().Wait(), ReceiveAsync().Wait()). This is the sync-over-async anti-pattern the framework conventions warn against; .Wait() wraps any exception in AggregateException (so the try/catch + rethrow at line 46-49 rethrows AggregateException, not the underlying WebSocketException), and on a captured SynchronizationContext it can deadlock. The AbstractPort contract is synchronous so some blocking is unavoidable, but ConfigureAwait(false) + GetAwaiter().GetResult() should be used to avoid AggregateException wrapping and reduce deadlock risk.
- **Fix:** Replace .Wait()/.Result with .ConfigureAwait(false).GetAwaiter().GetResult() so the original exception type propagates and the captured context is not required.

### CR-M078 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Contracts
- **Title:** RetryPolicy.GetDelay can overflow to a negative TimeSpan for large attemptNumber/multiplier
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Contracts\Retry/RetryPolicy.cs:56-58`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — GetDelay now computes the scaled delay in double and saturates at MaxDelay before casting (`scaled >= MaxDelay.Ticks || double.IsNaN(scaled) ? MaxDelay : FromTicks((long)scaled)`), so high attempt numbers can no longer overflow to a negative TimeSpan. Regression test (new Birko.Contracts.Tests) asserts GetDelay(53/100/1000/int.MaxValue) is >= 0 and == MaxDelay.
- **Detail:** delay = TimeSpan.FromTicks(BaseDelay.Ticks * (long)Math.Pow(BackoffMultiplier, attemptNumber - 1)). For a moderately high attemptNumber (e.g. with default BaseDelay=5s and BackoffMultiplier=2.0, around attempt 53+), Math.Pow exceeds long.MaxValue and the cast to long becomes long.MinValue (a large negative), or the subsequent multiply overflows in an unchecked context, producing a negative ticks value. The clamp 'if (delay > MaxDelay) delay = MaxDelay' only catches the upper bound — a negative delay is less than MaxDelay and passes through unclamped, so a retry-aware caller (BackgroundJobs, MessageQueue) gets a negative TimeSpan, which Task.Delay rejects with ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Because the saturation is meant to cap at MaxDelay anyway, the safe form is to compute in double and compare against MaxDelay before converting: e.g. compute factor=Math.Pow(...); if BaseDelay.Ticks*factor exceeds MaxDelay.Ticks (or is non-finite) return MaxDelay.
- **Fix:** Compute the scaled delay in double and saturate at MaxDelay before casting to ticks: var scaled = BaseDelay.Ticks * Math.Pow(BackoffMultiplier, attemptNumber - 1); delay = (double.IsNaN(scaled) || scaled >= MaxDelay.Ticks) ? MaxDelay : TimeSpan.FromTicks((long)scaled);

### CR-M082 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Core
- **Title:** CopyTo returns null when called with no argument despite non-null contract

- **Detail:** AbstractModel.CopyTo(AbstractModel? clone = null) returns `clone!`. When called as `model.CopyTo()` (the default), clone is null and the method returns null at runtime while the signature and the ICopyable<T> contract (`T CopyTo(T clone)`, non-nullable) promise a non-null result. ### CR-M084 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.CosmosDB
- **Title:** Aggregation GROUP BY/SELECT use property names verbatim — likely case mismatch with stored fields
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.CosmosDB\Aggregation/CosmosAggregationHelper.cs:50,55,62`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — CosmosAggregationHelper now emits bracket-quoted identifiers via a `FieldRef` helper (`c["Field"]`) for the SELECT group-by columns, aggregate source fields, and the GROUP BY clause, escaping embedded quotes/backslashes so a field name can no longer inject or break SQL shape. Tests (Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Tests) assert the bracket-quoted output, COUNT(1), the escaping, and null/empty→`c`.
- **Detail:** BuildAggregateSqlParts emits `c.{fieldName}` and `c.{sourceProperty}` straight from the model property names (PascalCase, e.g. c.Value). The rest of the store serializes models with default System.Text.Json (no camelCase policy is configured), so stored fields are PascalCase too — which happens to align here — but this only works by coincidence. If any consumer configures a camelCase CosmosSerializer (the common Cosmos convention) the aggregate SQL silently returns nulls/zeros because c.Value != c.value. There is no escaping/validation of field names either, so an attacker-influenced GroupByField name is interpolated raw into SQL.
- **Fix:** Resolve aggregate/group-by field names through the same naming policy used for serialization (or document that PascalCase serialization is required), and bracket-quote identifiers (c["Field"]) to avoid SQL-shape surprises.

### CR-M085 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.CosmosDB
- **Title:** IndexManager Exists/Drop key matching is inconsistent with Create's path normalization
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.CosmosDB\IndexManagement/CosmosDBIndexManager.cs:40,68,114,120-123`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — Extracted shared normalization/matching helpers (`NormalizeIncludedPath` → `/name/?`, `NormalizeFieldPath` → `/name`, `IncludedPathMatches`, `FieldPathMatches`, `PolicyContainsIndex`, `RemoveIncludedIndex`). CreateAsync/ExistsAsync/DropAsync/GetInfoAsync now all go through them: Exists/GetInfo match the normalized (or raw) form so an index created by name is found; Drop removes the matched path and mirrors *that* path into ExcludedPaths only when something was actually removed (no more stray raw ExcludedPath). Tests (Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Tests) cover the helpers against a constructed IndexingPolicy (included + composite match, remove-and-exclude, no-match-excludes-nothing).
- **Detail:** CreateAsync normalizes a single-field index path to `/{name}/?` (lines 62-66) and stores it in IncludedPaths. But ExistsAsync compares `p.Path == indexName` (line 40) against the raw, un-normalized indexName, so an index created via CreateAsync (path '/Foo/?') will never be reported as existing when checked by name 'Foo'. DropAsync has the same mismatch: it tries to remove IncludedPaths by raw indexName (line 114, won't match the normalized stored path) and then unconditionally adds the raw indexName to ExcludedPaths (lines 120-123) — pushing an invalid, non-normalized path into the policy regardless of whether anything was removed. ListAsync surfaces the normalized '/Foo/?' as the Name, so GetInfoAsync(name) (which compares against ListAsync output) also won't match a caller's plain field name.
- **Fix:** Apply the same path-normalization in ExistsAsync/DropAsync before comparing/removing, and only add to ExcludedPaths the normalized path that was actually present. Make GetInfoAsync match on the normalized form.

### CR-M086 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Views
- **Title:** Filter translator emits invalid/injectable SQL for DateTime, enum, and other types
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Views\CosmosViewStore.cs:415-425`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — TranslateValue (in CosmosFilterTranslator) gained explicit cases: DateTime/DateTimeOffset are ISO-8601 quoted (`'…o…'`, matching System.Text.Json's default) and enums emit their numeric value (default serialization), instead of the culture-dependent unquoted ToString() that produced invalid SQL. (string escaping already used the correct Cosmos backslash form and bool/number/decimal/Guid/null were already handled — improved since the audit snapshot.) Tests (Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Views.Tests) cover DateTime/DateTimeOffset/enum/string-escape/bool/number/Guid/null.
- **Detail:** TranslateValue's switch only quotes string and Guid; the fallback '_ => value.ToString()!' emits an unquoted token for any other type. A DateTime filter value yields e.g. 'c.Created = 6/17/2026 12:00:00 AM' (invalid SQL); enums emit the member name unquoted; arbitrary objects ToString() raw. Also string escaping uses \' which is not the Cosmos convention (Cosmos string literals escape an embedded single quote per JSON/SQL rules), so a value containing a quote can break the literal or inject. Because Translate() wraps everything in try/catch returning string.Empty, a broken literal that does not throw produces a silently malformed WHERE rather than an error.
- **Fix:** Use parameterized QueryDefinition.WithParameter for all values instead of string interpolation (eliminates injection and type-formatting bugs at once), or at minimum quote DateTime as ISO-8601 string, handle enums, and use correct Cosmos string escaping. Add tests for DateTime and quote-containing string filters.

### CR-M088 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.ElasticSearch
- **Title:** EnumerableExtensions.MultiMatch / MoreLikeThis is broken, dead code
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.ElasticSearch\Extensions/EnumerableExtensions.cs:15`
- **Category:** cleanup · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — MultiMatch/MoreLikeThis are kept as query-DSL **marker** methods (they are recognized by name in ElasticSearch.ParseExpression and translated to Nest queries; removing them would break filter expressions that reference them) but now have throw-only bodies (`NotSupportedException` with a clear "marker method" message) instead of the broken `Compile()`-a-parameter-expression bodies. A MemberExpression like `x.Name` references a lambda parameter, so Compile() on it as a parameterless Func<string> will throw at runtime ('variable of type ... referenced from scope but is not defined'). These are clearly meant to be expression-tree *marker* methods (ParseExpression in ElasticSearch.cs matches a MethodCall named "MultiMatch" by name and never invokes this extension), so the bodies are nonsensical and never correctly executed. The method also shadows the marker name used in query parsing, which is confusing.
- **Fix:** Remove this file (or, if MultiMatch/MoreLikeThis are intended as query DSL markers, give them throw-only bodies like `throw new NotSupportedException("marker method, use only inside store filter expressions")` and document them).

- **Title:** Manager and Store resolve the view index name with different rules

### CR-M094 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.InfluxDB
- **Title:** SaveAsync update path bypasses lazy-init and retry, diverging from every other operation
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.InfluxDB\Stores/AsyncInfluxDBStore.cs:269-288`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — SaveAsync's update branch now delegates to `UpdateAsync(data, processDelegate, ct)` (mirroring the create branch's use of `CreateAsync`), so the update observes `EnsureInitializedAsync` + `ExecuteWithRetryAsync` like every other CRUD path — no more direct WritePointAsync that skipped lazy-init and lost transient-failure retry. Verified via the InfluxDB.Tests build (the store compiles + existing/new tests green).
- **Detail:** SaveAsync is a public override that never calls EnsureInitializedAsync, so the create branch relies on CreateAsync to initialize but the update branch (data.Guid set) writes the point directly via Client.GetWriteApiAsync().WritePointAsync(...) with no EnsureInitializedAsync gate and no ExecuteWithRetryAsync wrapper. This means a Save-update against a not-yet-initialized store can target a missing bucket, and it loses the transient-failure retry behavior that CreateCoreAsync/UpdateCoreAsync all have. The two branches are inconsistent. Also note it ignores the configured RetryPolicy on this path only.
- **Fix:** Route the update branch through UpdateAsync (or at least EnsureInitializedAsync + ExecuteWithRetryAsync) so Save observes lazy-init and retry like every other CRUD method, mirroring the create branch's use of CreateAsync.

### CR-M096 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.InfluxDB.ViewModel
- **Title:** Destroy()/DestroyAsync() destroys the underlying store twice (bucket dropped twice)
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.InfluxDB.ViewModel\Repositories/AsyncInfluxDBRepository.cs:85-92 (and InfluxDBRepository.cs:79-83)`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — removed the `DestroyAsync`/`Destroy` overrides on both `AsyncInfluxDBRepository` and `InfluxDBRepository`; the base already destroys the store, and the overrides also called `DropAsync`/`Drop` (the same unwrapped store) → the bucket was dropped an extra time per Destroy. The distinct public `DropAsync`/`Drop` methods are kept for callers that want an explicit drop. New Birko.Data.InfluxDB.ViewModel.Tests asserts (structurally) the overrides are gone while Drop/DropAsync remain. (Note: the base bulk repo itself calls the store's DestroyAsync via both `Store` and `BulkStore` — the same instance — so it destroys twice; that pre-existing base behavior is a separate concern, out of scope for this finding which is about the InfluxDB layer's extra drop.)
- **Detail:** The base AbstractAsyncBulkViewModelRepository.DestroyAsync already calls BulkStore.DestroyAsync(ct) (see Birko.Data.ViewModel/Repositories/AbstractAsyncBulkViewModelRepository.cs:167-174), and the sync base AbstractViewModelRepository.Destroy already calls Store?.Destroy() (AbstractViewModelRepository.cs:251-254). The override here calls base.DestroyAsync(ct) AND THEN DropAsync(ct), which calls InfluxDBStore.DestroyAsync — the same unwrapped store. So DestroyAsync is invoked twice on the identical store instance. For an InfluxDB store DestroyAsync drops the bucket, so the bucket-drop runs twice per Destroy. Depending on the store's idempotency this is at best wasted work / a double round-trip and at worst a second drop that errors or races. The async override is also redundant with the base purely to call Drop again.
- **Fix:** Drop the override entirely (the base already destroys the store), or if a distinct Drop() public method is wanted, do not also invoke it from the Destroy/DestroyAsync override. If the override must stay for the doc-comment, remove the second DropAsync(ct)/Drop() call so the store is destroyed exactly once.

### CR-M100 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Localization
- **Title:** Create/Update/Delete(IEnumerable<T>) enumerate the source sequence twice
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Localization\Decorators/LocalizedBulkStoreWrapper.cs:138-160,179-186 and Decorators/AsyncLocalizedBulkStoreWrapper.cs:145-167,188-195`

### CR-M103 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.CosmosDB

### CR-M104 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.CosmosDB
- **Title:** ParseFilterToSql builds SQL by string interpolation of field names
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.CosmosDB\Context/CosmosDBDataMigrator.cs:139`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — ParseFilterToSql now emits bracket-quoted identifiers `c["{name}"]` (embedded quotes/backslashes escaped) instead of the raw dotted `c.{name}`, so a field name with whitespace/special chars can't produce malformed or injectable SQL (values were already escaped; identifiers now are too). Tests (Birko.Data.Migrations.CosmosDB.Tests) updated to the bracket-quoted output + a special-char/embedded-quote case.
- **Detail:** Field names from the filter JSON are interpolated directly into the SQL text as `c.{property.Name}` (line 139) with no validation or quoting. Values are escaped (FormatSqlValue doubles single quotes), but field names are not — a property name containing whitespace or SQL syntax produces malformed/injectable queries. Since filterJson is typically migration-author-supplied this is low real-world risk, but the asymmetry (values escaped, identifiers not) is a latent correctness hole; identifiers with special chars should use bracket quoting c["name"].
- **Fix:** Emit `c["{property.Name}"]` (with the name escaped for embedded quotes) instead of `c.{property.Name}` so arbitrary field names are handled safely and uniformly.

### CR-M105 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.ElasticSearch
- **Title:** GetAppliedVersions caps the search at 1000 documents
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.ElasticSearch\ElasticSearchMigrationStore.cs:75-86`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — GetAppliedVersions now sorts **Descending** and raises the window to 10000 (the default index.max_result_window), so a truncated result keeps the newest versions and GetCurrentVersion() (which takes Max()) can no longer under-report by dropping the highest versions past 1000. A deployment exceeding 10k applied migrations would need scroll (documented inline). Code-review verified (needs a live ES to exercise).
- **Detail:** GetAppliedVersions issues a single Search with `.Size(1000)`. Past 1000 applied migrations the result set is silently truncated. Because GetCurrentVersion() derives the current version from versions.Max() over this truncated set, and the sort is Ascending, the highest applied versions are exactly the ones dropped — GetCurrentVersion would under-report and the runner would re-execute already-applied migrations.
- **Fix:** Either fetch only the max via an aggregation / single descending Size(1) query for GetCurrentVersion, or page/scroll for the full set. At minimum sort Descending so a truncated window keeps the newest versions.

### CR-M106 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.ElasticSearch
- **Title:** RecordMigration does not refresh the migrations index
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.ElasticSearch\ElasticSearchMigrationStore.cs:114-119`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — RecordMigration's Index and RemoveMigration's Delete now pass `.Refresh(Elasticsearch.Net.Refresh.True)`, so an applied-version read immediately after (a second Migrate()/GetPendingMigrations() in the same process) sees the just-recorded/removed version and won't re-execute the migration. (The async variants delegate to the sync ones, so both are covered.) Code-review verified (needs a live ES).
- **Detail:** RecordMigration indexes the migration doc without a refresh. ES is near-real-time (default 1s refresh_interval), so a GetCurrentVersion()/GetAppliedVersions() search performed immediately after — e.g. a second Migrate() call in the same process, or GetPendingMigrations() right after running — may not see the just-recorded version and could re-execute the migration. DataMigrator.BulkInsert/CopyData explicitly call Indices.Refresh for exactly this reason, but the state store does not.
- **Fix:** Add `.Refresh(Elasticsearch.Net.Refresh.True)` to the Index call (and to RemoveMigration's Delete), so applied-version reads are immediately consistent.

### CR-M108 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB
- **Title:** Sync-over-async (.GetAwaiter().GetResult()) throughout blocks threads and can deadlock
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB\InfluxMigrationStore.cs:38,47,82; Context/InfluxDBSchemaBuilder.cs:29,43,81; Context/InfluxDBDataMigrator.cs:34,63,94`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open — deferred. The `IDataMigrator` interface (UpdateDocuments/DeleteDocuments/CopyData/BulkInsert/CountDocuments) is synchronous while the InfluxDB SDK is async-only, so the sync-over-async in the data migrator can't be removed without adding async members to the shared migration interfaces — the same interface-surface work as CR-M101 (CancellationToken threading). Best handled together in that dedicated async/CancellationToken batch rather than a blind per-backend rewrite. The store's async members (InitializeAsync etc.) can become genuinely async as part of that change.
- **Detail:** Every InfluxDB SDK call (FindBucketsAsync, CreateBucketAsync, QueryAsync, DeleteBucketAsync) is the async API blocked synchronously with .GetAwaiter().GetResult(). The async surface (InitializeAsync, RecordMigrationAsync, GetAppliedVersionsAsync, RemoveMigrationAsync, GetCurrentVersionAsync) just wraps the sync method in Task.FromResult / Task.CompletedTask, so there is no real async path and the SDK's native async is wasted. This blocks pool threads and risks deadlock in a captured-context host.
- **Fix:** Provide genuine async implementations that await the SDK calls and have the sync methods delegate or call the SDK's sync overloads, rather than fake-async wrappers over blocking calls.

### CR-M109 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB
- **Title:** CountDocuments double-aggregates (count() then sum()) — but per-table records make the result fragile
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB\Context/InfluxDBDataMigrator.cs:52-81`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open — deferred. The correct fix (restrict to one `_field` before `count()`, or pivot rows) changes the Flux pipeline in ways that need a live InfluxDB to validate against real multi-field measurements; getting it wrong silently changes counts. Better done alongside the InfluxDB-migration async rework (CR-M108) with an integration harness than tuned blind. Documented here as a known point-field-vs-row ambiguity.
- **Detail:** The flux pipeline does `count() |> group() |> sum()` to collapse per-series counts into one total. After group()+sum() InfluxDB yields a single record whose value is the summed long. The loop then also sums across all returned records (total += l). If the query returns more than one record (e.g. multiple fields per point are counted separately before group), the count is inflated because each point contributes one count per field, not per row. For a row-count this over-counts when measurements have multiple fields. The semantics of 'documents' vs InfluxDB points/fields is ambiguous and likely wrong for multi-field measurements.
- **Fix:** Restrict to a single field (e.g. pivot or filter to one _field) before count(), or document that the count is point-field count, not row count, to avoid silently wrong results.

### CR-M110 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB
- **Title:** CopyData coerces every non-string field to double, losing/corrupting int/bool/long fields
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB\Context/InfluxDBDataMigrator.cs:110-113; BulkInsert 142-145`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — extracted an `ApplyValue(point, key, value)` helper that preserves the value's runtime type: strings → tags; bool / integer types / floating-point → their matching Field overload; null skipped; anything else (DateTime, byte[]) → a string field instead of `Convert.ToDouble` throwing. CopyData and BulkInsert both use it, and CopyData now preserves the original `_time` via `record.GetTimeInDateTime()` + `.Timestamp(..., Ns)` (BulkInsert honors a `_time`/`time` DateTime in the document) instead of re-stamping to write time. Offline tests (Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB.Tests) assert bool/int/double/string/null/DateTime emission via ToLineProtocol.
- **Detail:** In CopyData and BulkInsert, any non-string value is written via Convert.ToDouble(entry.Value). Boolean fields, integer fields, and string-typed fields that happen to be numeric all collapse to double; booleans become 0/1 doubles, and Convert.ToDouble throws (FormatException) on non-numeric, non-bool objects (e.g. DateTime, byte[]). This silently changes field types on copy and can throw mid-migration, leaving InfluxDB in the inconsistent state the runner warns about. Also note _time is dropped (lines 107 / 139), so copied/inserted points get write-time timestamps rather than the original time — copied time-series data is re-stamped to 'now'.
- **Fix:** Branch on the actual runtime type (long/int/double/bool/string) and call the matching PointData.Field overload; preserve the original _time via .Timestamp(record.GetTime(), WritePrecision.Ns). Do not blanket Convert.ToDouble.

### CR-M111 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB
- **Title:** DeleteDocuments / RemoveMigration pass a raw filter string through as a Flux delete predicate with no validation or escaping
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB\Context/InfluxDBDataMigrator.cs:44-48,154-158; InfluxMigrationStore.cs:152,159`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** done — `ConvertFilterToFluxPredicate` now rejects a JSON filter (input starting with `{`) with a clear `NotSupportedException` (empty/`{}` → "", a real Flux predicate string still passes through) instead of forwarding invalid JSON as the delete predicate. `RemoveMigration` escapes the interpolated `migration.Name` via a new `EscapeFluxString` helper so a quote/backslash can't break the predicate. Offline tests cover the empty/JSON/passthrough branches + the escaper. (The unconditional -100y..now delete range is a separate concern left as-is.)
- **Detail:** ConvertFilterToFluxPredicate returns filterJson verbatim, so a JSON filter ({"x":1}) is sent as the Influx delete predicate, which is NOT JSON — it must be a predicate like `_measurement="m" AND tag="v"`. Any non-empty filterJson that isn't already a valid delete predicate will either error or, worse, fail to match and silently delete nothing / everything in range. RemoveMigration interpolates migration.Name directly into the predicate (line 152) with no escaping, so a name containing a quote breaks the predicate. The DeleteDocuments range also spans -100y to now unconditionally.
- **Fix:** Either properly translate the JSON filter to a Flux delete predicate or reject non-empty filters with a clear exception; escape interpolated values (migration.Name) in RemoveMigration.

Offline tests (Birko.Data.Migrations.MongoDB.Tests) assert no-transform → just `$merge`, single stage prepended, and an array prepended in order.

A migration author passing a transform (e.g. a $project/$addFields stage) gets a straight copy with no transform applied and no error, which can produce silently wrong data in the target collection. transformJson is also not validated.
- **Fix:** If transformJson is provided, parse it (BsonDocument.Parse) and insert the corresponding aggregation stage(s) before the $merge stage; otherwise document and assert that transforms are unsupported (throw NotSupportedException when transformJson is non-empty) rather than silently dropping it.

### CR-M117 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.MongoDB
- **Title:** Public Read(Guid)/Read() overrides bypass lazy-init

### CR-M118 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.MongoDB
- **Title:** Async ReadAsync(Guid) override bypasses lazy-init and cancellation gate
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.MongoDB\Stores/AsyncMongoDBStore.cs:88-97`
- **Category:** convention · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** AsyncMongoDBStore overrides public ReadAsync(Guid) to call Collection.Find(...).FirstOrDefaultAsync directly. The base ReadAsync(Guid) delegates to ReadAsync(filter), which calls EnsureInitializedAsync(ct) — that gate also now performs ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested() per the 2026-06-15 cancellation change. This override skips both init and the cancellation observation, so an already-cancelled token is not honored on this path and InitCoreAsync never runs before a by-Guid read. It is also redundant (base routes through ReadCoreAsync).
- **Fix:** Remove the override; the base ReadAsync(Guid) -> ReadAsync(filter) -> ReadCoreAsync path already covers it with correct init/cancellation behavior.

### CR-M119 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.MongoDB
- **Title:** SaveAsync/Save override's upsert path bypasses lazy-init
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.MongoDB\Stores/AsyncMongoDBStore.cs:198-219`
- **Category:** convention · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open

If a caller's first interaction with the store is Save on an entity that already has a Guid, InitCoreAsync never runs and cancellation is not observed. (InitCoreAsync is currently a no-op for MongoDB, so impact is low today, but it breaks the contract for subclasses that add real init.)

### CR-M122 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.MongoDB.Views

### CR-M124 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Patterns
- **Title:** Slug/SoftDelete/Audit/Timestamp bulk wrappers enumerate the input IEnumerable multiple times
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Patterns\Decorators/AsyncSluggableBulkStoreWrapper.cs:30`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** AsyncSluggableBulkStoreWrapper.CreateAsync (lines 30-35) iterates `data` in a foreach to resolve/mutate slugs, then passes the same `data` to `_innerStore.CreateAsync(data, ...)`, enumerating it a second time. SluggableBulkStoreWrapper.Create/Update (SluggableBulkStoreWrapper.cs:26-38) do the same. If `data` is a deferred/lazy LINQ sequence that yields fresh object instances per enumeration, the mutations made on the first pass (Slug assignment, and likewise DeletedAt in the SoftDelete Delete overload AsyncSoftDeleteBulkStoreWrapper.cs:59, CreatedBy/UpdatedBy via Select projections in the Audit/Timestamp bulk wrappers) are observed on objects that are then discarded, and the second enumeration persists unmutated objects. The Select-based wrappers (Audit/Timestamp) are safer only because the projection re-applies on the single enumeration the inner store performs, but the slug/softdelete foreach-then-pass pattern is genuinely wrong for non-materialized inputs.
- **Fix:** Materialize once at the top of each bulk method: `var items = data as IList<T> ?? data.ToList();` then operate on and pass `items`. AsyncDefaultStoreWrapper already does this correctly with `data.ToList()` — apply the same pattern uniformly.

### CR-M125 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Patterns
- **Title:** Versioned wrapper update is read-check-write with no concurrency guard, and unconditionally skips the check when entity is absent
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Patterns\Concurrency/AsyncVersionedStoreWrapper.cs:43`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** UpdateAsync reads the existing row, compares versions, then increments and writes. Two concerns: (1) The version check only fires `if (existing != null ...)`. If the read returns null (row not yet visible, wrong guid, or a store that returns null transiently), the conflict check is skipped entirely and the write proceeds with data.Version++ — a lost-update window rather than the intended optimistic failure. (2) The whole read-then-write is non-atomic at the wrapper level, so this only narrows, not closes, the concurrency window; the actual version match must be enforced in the inner store's WHERE/$match for real protection. At minimum, document that this provides best-effort detection only, and consider treating a null read as a conflict (or a not-found) rather than a silent pass. Same logic in the sync VersionedStoreWrapper.cs:41.
- **Fix:** Decide explicit semantics for the missing-row case (throw ConcurrentUpdateException or a NotFound) and document that true optimistic locking requires the inner store to include the version in its update predicate.

### CR-M128 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Processors
- **Title:** ProcessStreamAsync on CSV does blocking synchronous I/O (fake async)
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Processors\Formats/CsvProcessor.cs:92`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** ProcessStreamAsync iterates parser.Parse(), which is a synchronous IEnumerable that does blocking reader.Read() on the underlying stream. The method is declared async but performs sync-over-async blocking I/O on the calling thread (only the per-row callbacks and the cancellation check are async). For an HTTP/network-backed stream this blocks a thread per parse. The framework convention is that async methods do real async work. The cancellation token is observed between rows, so functionally it works, but it is not genuinely asynchronous.
- **Fix:** Either document that CSV parsing is inherently synchronous, or add an async parse path (StreamReader.ReadLineAsync / IAsyncEnumerable) so the async overload doesn't block. At minimum avoid presenting it as non-blocking.

### CR-M129 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Processors
- **Title:** XmlReader async mode reads node value via synchronous Value getter

With Async=true, the synchronous Value property can throw InvalidOperationException when the value isn't fully buffered (large text/CDATA), because the async reader expects GetValueAsync(). Tests only cover tiny inline values so this latent failure is not exercised.

### CR-M134 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL
- **Title:** InitException swallows exceptions then continues executing on a bad command
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL\SQL/Connectors/AbstractConnector.cs:32-42, 244-256; AbstractAsyncConnector.cs:136-150`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** When an OnException handler is registered, InitException invokes it and RETURNS (does not rethrow). In the reader paths (RunReaderCommand / RunReaderCommandAsync), the try/catch around createCommand+OnExecute is followed unconditionally by command.ExecuteReader(). If createCommand threw (e.g. bad expression, missing field) the handler runs but execution falls through to ExecuteReader on a malformed/empty command, producing a second, more confusing error or silently wrong results. The default (no handler) path rethrows, so this only bites consumers who set OnException — but those are exactly the callers expecting the handler to terminate the operation.
- **Fix:** After InitException handles a createCommand failure, short-circuit (yield break / return) instead of proceeding to ExecuteReader. Track a 'faulted' flag from the catch and guard the ExecuteReader call.

### CR-M137 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.MSSql
- **Title:** DbType.Object/Binary map to fixed-length BINARY with no length (BINARY(1))

### CR-M138 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.MSSql
- **Title:** BulkInsert/Update/Delete swallow exceptions via InitException after rollback
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL.MSSql\Database/Connector/MSSqlConnector.cs:288-291, 383-387, 506-510`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The non-cancel catch blocks call InitException(ex, ...) and then return normally, so on a genuine failure (e.g. constraint violation, type mismatch from the TINYINT issue above) the bulk method completes as if it succeeded - the caller (CreateCore/UpdateCore/DeleteCore) gets no exception and assumes the rows were written. ### CR-M142 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.PostgreSQL
- **Title:** FieldDefinition SERIAL substitution can corrupt VARCHAR(n)/NUMERIC columns whose length/precision contains the type token
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL.PostgreSQL\Database\Connectors\PostgreSQLConnector.cs:179-206`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** Auto-increment handling does a textual String.Replace on the already-built field definition (e.g. sqlType.Replace("INTEGER", "SERIAL")). This only fires when field.Type is an integer type, so in practice the column type is INTEGER/BIGINT/SMALLINT and the replace is safe today. The fragility is that it operates on the whole definition string rather than the type token: if a future field name or any appended fragment ever contained the substring (or if the guard were loosened), Replace would mutate it. The robust form is to choose SERIAL vs INTEGER when emitting ConvertType, not to post-process the string. Low real-world risk given current guards, but it is brittle string surgery.
- **Fix:** Emit SERIAL/BIGSERIAL/SMALLSERIAL directly when field.IsAutoincrement at the point ConvertType result is appended, instead of String.Replace on the composed definition.

### CR-M144 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite
- **Title:** Bulk operations bypass transient-error retry (ExecuteWithRetry), defeating the connector's own IsTransientException
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite\Database\Connectors\SqLiteConnector.cs:219`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The connector overrides IsTransientException to flag SQLITE_BUSY (5) and SQLITE_LOCKED (6) — exactly the errors a retry policy exists to handle for concurrent SQLite access. But BulkInsert/BulkUpdate/BulkDelete and their async variants open the connection, begin a transaction, and execute directly, with no ExecuteWithRetry wrapper. The base RunCommand/RunCommandTransaction (AbstractConnector.cs:167,199) wrap execution in ExecuteWithRetry. So under contention the native bulk ops fail immediately instead of retrying, even though the framework's retry policy and the connector's transient-detection were set up for it.
- **Fix:** Wrap the bulk command bodies in ExecuteWithRetry (or factor the open/transaction/execute into the same retry helper the base connector uses) so SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED are retried per the configured RetryPolicy.

### CR-M146 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite.View
- **Title:** ViewExistsAsync not overridden — async path uses inferior, view/table-confusing base probe
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite.View\Database\Connectors\SqLiteConnector_View.cs:17`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** SqLiteConnector derives from AbstractAsyncConnector (SqLiteConnector.cs:18), which declares its own virtual ViewExistsAsync (AbstractAsyncConnector_CreateView.cs:128) separate from the sync ViewExists. This project overrides only the sync ViewExists (line 17) to query sqlite_master WHERE type='view'. The async ViewExistsAsync is NOT overridden, so async callers (CreateViewIfNotExistsAsync at AbstractAsyncConnector_CreateView.cs:153, and Auto-mode existence checks via ShouldUsePersistentView) fall through to the base implementation, which runs 'SELECT 1 FROM "name" WHERE 1=0' inside a try/catch. That base probe (a) returns true for a same-named TABLE, not just a view — so CreateViewIfNotExistsAsync would wrongly skip creation when a table shadows the name — and (b) relies on catch-all exception control flow. The sync override was added specifically to avoid both problems; the async path silently lacks that correctness and optimization. (Note: all sibling .View projects — MSSql/MySQL/PostgreSQL — share this same gap, so it is a framework-wide consistency issue rather than unique to SQLite.)
- **Fix:** Add a 'public override async Task<bool> ViewExistsAsync(string viewName, CancellationToken ct = default)' that runs the same sqlite_master / type='view' parameterized query via DoCommandAsync + ExecuteReaderAsync(ct), mirroring the sync override and observing the cancellation token.

### CR-M147 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.View

So a caller passing an explicit view name like `new View(tables, joins, "OrderSummary")` silently gets the concatenated table-name string instead of "OrderSummary". The intent was almost certainly to derive a name only when none was supplied (i.e. `if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(name) && Tables.Any())`).

### CR-M148 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.View
- **Title:** GetViewField returns null! and the caller immediately dereferences it

Its callers in AbstractConnector_SelectView.cs:22 and :69 do `DataBase.GetViewField(x.Key).GetSelectName(true)` with no null check, so an order-by expression that doesn't map to a view field throws NullReferenceException instead of a meaningful error. Additionally line 61 casts `expr.Body` directly to UnaryExpression and line 62 casts `.Operand` to MemberExpression — a lambda whose body is a plain MemberExpression (no boxing conversion, e.g. `x => x.Name` on a reference type) will throw InvalidCastException.

### CR-M149 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.View
- **Title:** Auto-mode view-existence cache can be poisoned by transient failures and goes stale on external drops
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.SQL.View\SQL/Connectors/AbstractConnectorBase_View.cs:43; SQL/Connectors/AbstractConnector_CreateView.cs:124-143`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** ShouldUsePersistentView (Auto mode) caches the result of ViewExists via GetOrAdd. ViewExists probes with `SELECT 1 FROM view WHERE 1=0` and a bare `catch { return false; }`. A transient error (connection blip, lock timeout, permission hiccup) is indistinguishable from 'view absent', so a `false` gets cached permanently and the view is never used again for that name until ClearViewExistsCache is called. Conversely, if the view is created/dropped outside this connector instance, the cached `true`/`false` is never re-validated at query time (the documented 'fall back to on-the-fly if the view doesn't exist' only happens at the cached decision point, not per query). ViewExists also swallows genuine DB errors that callers might want surfaced.
- **Fix:** Don't cache negative results from a broad catch (only cache definitive existence), and/or narrow the catch to the provider's 'relation does not exist' error. Consider a short TTL on cached entries for Auto mode.

### CR-M153 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.SQL.Views
- **Title:** GroupBy clauses from ViewDefinition are silently dropped

- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** definition.GroupBy is read only inside CollectSourceTypes (to ensure the source table is loaded); it is never translated into any GROUP BY metadata on the resulting Tables.View. The connector (AbstractConnectorBase_View.BuildViewSelectSql:235-242 and CreateSelectCommand) instead auto-derives GROUP BY from all non-aggregate SELECTed fields. This happens to work only when every GroupByClause field is also present in definition.Fields. ### CR-M155 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Sync
- **Title:** Preview catch block swallows all exceptions including cancellation

- **Detail:** Preview/PreviewAsync wrap the whole body in try { ... } catch { preview.Conflicts++; return preview; }. Any failure (store read error, OperationCanceledException from the async ReadAsync token, NRE) is silently converted into a normal-looking SyncPreview with Conflicts incremented by one. ### CR-M172 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Tagging

- **Category:** cleanup · **Verification:** not individually verified

For each missing tag it calls AttachTagAsync (line 131), which at line 100 re-issues GetEntityTagLinksAsync(entityType, entityId, ct) and re-scans for duplicates. So a sync that adds N tags performs N extra link queries that are redundant — the diff was already computed against a known-not-present set. ### CR-M173 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Tenant
- **Title:** Bulk Update/Delete enumerate the source IEnumerable twice
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Tenant\Stores/TenantBulkStoreWrapper.cs:27-37,52-62 and Stores/AsyncTenantBulkStoreWrapper.cs:29-39,54-64`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** Delete(IEnumerable<T> data) / Update(IEnumerable<T> data) call data.All(BelongsToCurrentTenant) and then pass the same `data` to _innerStore.Delete/Update. `data` is enumerated twice. For a lazy/streaming/once-only enumerable (e.g. a yield iterator or a query) this re-runs the source, and if the sequence is non-deterministic the validated set differs from the persisted set — defeating the tenant authorization check. The same double-enumeration occurs in the async variants.
- **Fix:** Materialize once: `var list = data as IReadOnlyCollection<T> ?? data.ToList();` then validate and pass `list` to the inner store.

### CR-M174 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Tenant
- **Title:** SaveAsync discards CreateAsync return value and relies on the inner store mutating data.Guid
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Tenant\Stores/AsyncTenantStoreWrapper.cs:87-104`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** On the create branch SaveAsync calls `await CreateAsync(...)` but ignores the returned Guid, then returns `data.Guid ?? Guid.Empty`. This only yields the new id if the inner store mutates the passed entity's Guid in place (InMemory does via `data.Guid ??= Guid.NewGuid()`, but that is not guaranteed by the IAsyncStore contract — a store could allocate the id internally and return it without writing it back). The synchronous TenantStoreWrapper.Save (line 99) correctly returns the Create result directly, so the two wrappers are inconsistent and the async one is the fragile one.
- **Fix:** Mirror the sync wrapper: `return await CreateAsync(data, processDelegate, cancellationToken);` on the create branch.

### CR-M175 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.Tenant
- **Title:** Static Tenant.Current singleton coexists with DI-scoped ITenantContext as a second source of truth
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.Tenant\Models/TenantContext.cs:114-149; RepositoryServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:39,75,107,137; Stores/*StoreWrapper.cs ctor fallback`
- **Category:** other · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** Wrappers and DI factories fall back to `Models.Tenant.Current` (a process-wide static TenantContext) when no ITenantContext is supplied/registered. In an ASP.NET app the recommended registration is AddTenantContextScoped (a per-request DI instance), but TenantMiddleware sets the tenant on whichever ITenantContext was resolved from DI, while any store/repo accidentally constructed with the static fallback reads `Tenant.Current` — a different instance whose tenant was never set. This silently produces non-tenant-mode (unfiltered) access. The two parallel context sources are an easy mis-wiring footgun.
- **Fix:** Document that the static Tenant.Current is for non-DI/console scenarios only, and consider making the wrapper/factory fallback throw (or log) rather than silently substituting the static singleton when ITenantContext is expected from DI.

### CR-M179 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.ViewModel
- **Title:** Async bulk repository bypasses change-tracking (StoreHash) used by the single-item paths
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.ViewModel\Repositories/AbstractAsyncBulkViewModelRepository.cs:62-93, 105-110, 152-157`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** CreateAsync/UpdateAsync/DeleteAsync/ReadAsync inline `CreateModelInstance()+MapToModel` and `CreateInstance()+LoadFrom` instead of calling the base helpers LoadModelInstance/LoadInstance. As a result the async bulk read never calls StoreHash (the base LoadInstance stores the hash at AbstractAsyncViewModelRepository.cs:163), so the change-tracking dictionary is never populated for entities fetched via the bulk ReadAsync. A subsequent single-item UpdateAsync then sees no stored hash and CheckHashChange always returns true — the optimistic no-op-update skip is defeated. The sync bulk Read (AbstractBulkViewModelRepository.cs:48) correctly routes through LoadInstance. Make the async bulk path use LoadInstance/LoadModelInstance for consistency.
- **Fix:** Use `LoadInstance(model)` in ReadAsync and `LoadModelInstance(vm)` in CreateAsync/UpdateAsync/DeleteAsync so hashing and the ViewModel→Model mapping are applied uniformly.

### CR-M182 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.XML
- **Title:** EnsureDataLoadedAsync re-reads disk whenever the store is legitimately empty
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.XML\Stores\AbstractAsyncXmlStore.cs:124`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** EnsureDataLoadedAsync gates loading on `_items == null || _items.Count == 0`. A store that genuinely persists zero rows (empty file, or after all rows deleted) will hit LoadDataAsync on every single read/count/aggregate call, re-opening and re-deserializing the file each time. It also means: after deleting the last entity in-process, the next operation reloads from disk (harmless here since the file matches, but the flag-by-count approach is fragile). A dedicated boolean 'loaded' flag would be correct.

### CR-M183 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Data.XML
- **Title:** SaveData deletes file then OpenWrite — data loss window if write fails
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Data.XML\Stores\XmlStore.cs:225`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** SaveData does File.Delete(Path) then File.OpenWrite to rewrite the whole file (AsyncXmlStore.cs:238 deletes then FileMode.Create). If serialization throws between the delete and a complete write (e.g. a non-serializable property, cancellation, process kill), the existing data file is already gone and the new one is partial or absent — total data loss. The JSON reference store typically writes to a temp file and atomically replaces. Note File.Delete is also redundant in the async case since FileMode.Create already truncates.
- **Fix:** Write to a temp file then atomically move/replace the target (File.Replace or File.Move with overwrite); drop the explicit Delete before FileMode.Create.

### CR-M184 · 🟡 medium · Birko.EventBus
- **Title:** ErrorHandlingMode.Stop is not honored in parallel dispatch
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.EventBus\Local\InProcessEventBus.cs:148-169`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** InProcessEventBusOptions documents ErrorHandlingMode.Stop as 'Stop dispatching to remaining handlers on first failure'. DispatchSequentialAsync honors this (the catch filter only matches Continue, so a throw propagates and aborts the loop). But DispatchParallelAsync eagerly materializes ALL handler tasks via handlers.Select(async ...) before awaiting Task.WhenAll. Every handler is already launched (up to the semaphore limit) regardless of mode, so when one throws in Stop mode the remaining handlers are not stopped — they keep running to completion. The Stop contract only works for MaxConcurrency<=1.
- **Fix:** Either document that Stop only applies to sequential dispatch, or implement real cancellation in parallel mode (e.g. a linked CancellationTokenSource cancelled on first failure, with handlers observing the token), so Stop actually halts pending/queued handlers.

### CR-M185 · 🟡 medium · Birko.EventBus
- **Title:** Handler exceptions are silently swallowed; 'Log and continue' contract has no logger
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.EventBus\Local\InProcessEventBus.cs:141-144`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** InProcessEventBusOptions.ErrorHandlingMode.Continue is documented as 'Log and continue to the next handler. Default.' but the catch-when blocks in both DispatchSequentialAsync (line 141) and DispatchParallelAsync (line 158) have empty bodies — nothing is logged. There is no ILogger field on InProcessEventBus at all. In the default configuration a throwing handler vanishes with zero diagnostics, which is a serious operability problem for an event bus.
- **Fix:** Inject an optional ILogger (or an error callback / IEventErrorHandler) and log the swallowed exception with the event type and EventId, or correct the doc to state exceptions are silently dropped.

### CR-M186 · 🟡 medium · Birko.EventBus.EventSourcing
- **Title:** Original event timestamp (OccurredAt) and EventId are dropped during wrapping/replay
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.EventBus.EventSourcing\DomainEventPublished.cs:48-56`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** DomainEventPublished copies AggregateId, Version, EventType, EventData, Metadata, UserId from the source IEvent but NOT its OccurredAt or EventId. Because EventBase initializes `OccurredAt = DefaultClock.UtcNow` and `EventId = Guid.NewGuid()` at construction time, every wrapper gets the *current* time and a fresh id. For the EventReplayService paths (ReplayAggregateAsync/ReplayFromVersionAsync/ReplayAllFromAsync), this means projections/read models being rebuilt see the replay wall-clock time rather than the historical event time, and lose the original event identity — which defeats time-ordered or idempotent (dedup-by-EventId) projection rebuilding, the stated purpose of the replay service. The domain IEvent.OccurredAt and IEvent.EventId are available on the source but never used.
- **Fix:** Propagate the source event's timestamp/identity, e.g. set `OccurredAt = domainEvent.OccurredAt` (and consider mapping EventId or carrying it in a dedicated property) in the constructor, or document explicitly that DomainEventPublished.OccurredAt is the publish time and add a separate DomainOccurredAt field for the original time.

### CR-M188 · 🟡 medium · Birko.EventBus.MessageQueue
- **Title:** Synchronous blocking on async unsubscribe during Dispose
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.EventBus.MessageQueue\DistributedEventBus.cs:232-235`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** Dispose() calls sub.UnsubscribeAsync().GetAwaiter().GetResult() for each queue subscription. This is sync-over-async and can deadlock if disposed on a thread with a synchronization context, and blocks the disposing thread on potentially network-bound unsubscribe calls. ISubscription is IDisposable, and the type also has no IAsyncDisposable path.
- **Fix:** Implement IAsyncDisposable and await UnsubscribeAsync there; in synchronous Dispose, call sub.Dispose() (ISubscription : IDisposable) instead of blocking on the async method.

### CR-M189 · 🟡 medium · Birko.EventBus.Outbox
- **Title:** Reflection-invoked publish masks the real exception message on failure
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.EventBus.Outbox\Publishing/OutboxProcessor.cs:98-106 (PublishEventAsync) and :79-83 (catch)`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** PublishEventAsync uses MethodInfo.Invoke to call the generic PublishAsync. When the awaited Task faults the real exception surfaces correctly, but if MakeGenericMethod/Invoke itself throws (e.g. argument binding) it raises TargetInvocationException whose Message is the generic 'Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.' The catch at :79 records ex.Message into MarkFailedAsync, so LastError can be that uninformative wrapper instead of the underlying cause, hampering diagnosis of poison messages.
- **Fix:** Unwrap TargetInvocationException (use ex.InnerException?.Message ?? ex.Message, or rethrow the inner) before passing to MarkFailedAsync; consider recording ex.ToString() to capture the type.

### CR-M191 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Health.Azure
- **Title:** Catch-all swallows OperationCanceledException, breaking runner timeout handling
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Health.Azure\AzureBlobHealthCheck.cs:57 (and AzureKeyVaultHealthCheck.cs:57)`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The catch (Exception ex) block also catches OperationCanceledException/TaskCanceledException thrown by the awaited network call (storage.ListAsync / provider.ListSecretsAsync) when the token is cancelled or a timeout fires. HealthCheckRunner.RunCheckAsync (Birko.Health/Core/HealthCheckRunner.cs:85-100) creates a linked CTS with CancelAfter(timeout) and relies on the check letting OperationCanceledException bubble up: its 'catch (OperationCanceledException) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)' filter produces a proper 'Timed out after Xs' result honoring the registration's TimeoutStatus (which can be Degraded). Because these checks convert that cancellation into a generic Unhealthy('Azure ... failed: ...'), a check registered with TimeoutStatus = Degraded will still report Unhealthy on timeout, and the distinct timeout message/status is lost. Unlike the in-repo DiskSpaceHealthCheck (synchronous, ignores the token), these checks pass ct to a real async call, so the exception genuinely surfaces here.
- **Fix:** Rethrow cancellation before the generic catch, e.g. add 'catch (OperationCanceledException) { throw; }' above the 'catch (Exception ex)' block (or filter the generic catch with 'when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)'), so the runner's timeout-status logic applies. Confirm the framework's intended convention since the existing test CheckAsync_WhenCancelled_ReturnsUnhealthy currently asserts Unhealthy.

### CR-M192 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Health.Data
- **Title:** Internally-created HttpClient is never disposed (resource leak)
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Health.Data\ElasticSearchHealthCheck.cs:30 (also InfluxDbHealthCheck.cs:30, RavenDbHealthCheck.cs:30, VaultHealthCheck.cs:30, CosmosDbHealthCheck.cs:31, SseHealthCheck.cs:32)`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** When the optional httpClient ctor argument is null, each of the six HTTP checks does `_httpClient = httpClient ?? new HttpClient();` and stores it in a readonly field. The class is not IDisposable and never disposes that instance, so the socket-handler resources are leaked for the lifetime of the check object (and the underlying HttpMessageHandler / connection pool is never released). Health checks are typically long-lived singletons re-run on a timer, so a single leaked HttpClient per check is bounded, but the type still owns a disposable it created and never releases it — and it cannot distinguish an owned instance from a caller-supplied one to dispose correctly.
- **Fix:** Track ownership (e.g. bool _ownsClient = httpClient is null) and implement IDisposable to dispose the client only when owned; or use a single static shared HttpClient for the default case (the common ASP.NET guidance) so no per-instance handler is allocated. Mirror the disposal/ownership pattern used elsewhere in the framework for caller-vs-internally-created dependencies.

### CR-M193 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Health.Data
- **Title:** SMTP banner read can block indefinitely with no read timeout
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Health.Data\SmtpHealthCheck.cs:47`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** After TcpClient.ConnectAsync succeeds, the check awaits stream.ReadAsync(buffer, ct) to read the 220 banner. If the server completes the TCP handshake but never sends a banner (a hung/half-open SMTP server — a realistic failure mode the check is meant to detect), ReadAsync blocks until the CancellationToken fires. CheckAsync's default parameter is `ct = default`, so callers using the parameterless overload get no timeout at all and the health check hangs forever instead of reporting Unhealthy/Degraded. The same applies to the WriteAsync of QUIT.
- **Fix:** Apply a bounded timeout to the read (e.g. link a CancellationTokenSource with a timeout to ct, or set stream.ReadTimeout). This also lets the '>2000ms = Degraded' threshold actually mean something, since today a slow/silent server never returns.

### CR-M195 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Helpers
- **Title:** SanitizePath strips traversal patterns in a single non-recursive pass
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Helpers\PathValidator.cs:205`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The chained string.Replace calls for '../', '..\\', './', '.\\' run once each, so overlapping/nested sequences survive. E.g. '..././' -> removing './' yields '../'; '....//' style inputs can also re-form a traversal token after a single removal pass. The only backstop is the GetFullPath+StartsWith containment check in the callers, which is itself flawed (see the sibling-prefix finding), so a crafted userPath could slip through CombineAndValidate / CombineAndValidateUnchecked.

### CR-M197 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Localization

### CR-M198 · 🟡 medium · Birko.Localization.Data
- **Title:** Sync-over-async blocking can deadlock under a synchronous context
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.Localization.Data\DatabaseTranslationProvider.cs:57,114`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The synchronous ITranslationProvider members block on async store I/O via .GetAwaiter().GetResult(): GetCultureTranslations (line 114) and GetSupportedCultures via LoadAllAsync (line 57). If a caller invokes GetTranslation/GetAll/GetSupportedCultures on a thread with a single-threaded SynchronizationContext (legacy ASP.NET, WPF/WinForms UI thread) and the underlying store continuation needs that context, this deadlocks. Even without a deadlock it ties up a thread-pool thread for the duration of the store round-trip. The sync interface contract forces some form of this, so it cannot be fully eliminated here, but it is a real risk worth documenting.
- **Fix:** Document on the sync members that they block on store I/O and should be avoided on UI / single-threaded-sync-context threads; prefer GetTranslationAsync/GetAllAsync. Optionally guard the blocking calls with ConfigureAwait(false) inside the async helpers (already effectively the case since no context capture is needed) and steer consumers to the async API.

### CR-M200 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory
- **Title:** Old DispatchCts is cancelled but never disposed in RemoveSubscriber
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory\InMemoryChannel.cs:95`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** When the last subscriber is removed, state.DispatchCts?.Cancel() then state.DispatchCts = null. The CancellationTokenSource is an IDisposable and is dropped without Dispose(). If subscribers are added and removed repeatedly for the same destination, a new CTS is allocated each time (StartDispatching, line 108) and the previous ones are never disposed.

### CR-M201 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory
- **Title:** Delayed SendAsync is fire-and-forget and swallows write failures
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory\InMemoryProducer.cs:29`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** When message.Delay is set, the method spawns _ = Task.Run(...) and returns immediately. Any exception thrown by Task.Delay (e.g. the token is cancelled) or by _channel.WriteAsync (e.g. the bounded channel is completed/disposed) is raised on an unobserved task that no one awaits — it is silently lost. The caller's await SendAsync(...) completes successfully even though the message may never be enqueued. This is the sync-over-async / swallowed-exception anti-pattern called out in the framework conventions.
- **Fix:** At minimum attach a continuation that observes/logs the fault, or document that delayed sends are best-effort. Consider scheduling delayed delivery inside the channel rather than detaching an untracked task.

### CR-M202 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory
- **Title:** RejectAsync(requeue: true) silently discards the message instead of redelivering
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory\InMemoryConsumer.cs:83`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** RejectAsync removes the message from _pendingAck and, when requeue is true, the body of the if is empty (only a comment: the consumer cannot recover the destination, so the message is dropped). The public contract implies requeue:true should make the message available for redelivery; here both requeue:true and requeue:false behave identically (discard). Callers relying on requeue for poison-message handling get silent message loss.
- **Fix:** Track the originating destination alongside the pending-ack entry (store a (destination, message) tuple keyed by Id) so requeue can call _channel.WriteAsync(destination, message). If requeue genuinely cannot be supported in-memory, throw NotSupportedException rather than silently succeeding.

### CR-M203 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.MQTT
- **Title:** Race in EnsureEventAttached can attach the message handler twice
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.MessageQueue.MQTT\MqttConsumer.cs:91-100`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** _eventAttached is a plain (non-volatile) bool read then written without synchronization. SubscribeAsync is async and can be invoked concurrently from multiple threads; two callers can both observe _eventAttached == false and both execute `_client.ApplicationMessageReceivedAsync += OnMessageReceivedAsync`, double-subscribing the delegate. Every received message would then dispatch to each matching handler twice. Dispose removes the handler only once, leaving a dangling subscription.
- **Fix:** Guard the check-and-set with a lock, or use Interlocked.CompareExchange on an int flag, before subscribing to the event.

### CR-M204 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.MQTT
- **Title:** Subscriptions are not restored after auto-reconnect
- **Path:** `C:\Source\Birko\Framework\Birko.MessageQueue.MQTT\MqttMessageQueue.cs:145-169`
- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
- **Status:** open
- **Detail:** The reconnect loop calls ConnectAsync again, but it never re-issues the broker SUBSCRIBE for the topics held in MqttConsumer._handlers. With CleanSession=true (the documented default at MqttSettings.cs:38) the broker drops all subscriptions on disconnect, so after a reconnect the consumer keeps its in-memory handlers but receives nothing — silent message loss. The handler dictionary is the natural source to replay subscriptions on the ConnectedAsync event.
- **Fix:** On (re)connect, have the consumer re-subscribe all topics in _handlers (e.g. expose a ResubscribeAllAsync invoked from OnConnectedAsync), or delegate reconnection to MQTTnet's ManagedClient which replays subscriptions.

### CR-M206 · 🟡 medium · Birko.MessageQueue.Redis
- **Title:** CancellationToken ignored in producer and consumer Redis calls

- **Category:** bug · **Verification:** not individually verified
