## Per-project summaries

- **Birko.AI** (8): A small, generally well-structured agent/provider library whose main risks are a real process-output deadlock in RunCommandTool, sync-over-async blocking and missing cancellation/disposal in the streaming agent loop, plus a complete absence of a test project.
- **Birko.AI.Agents** (2): A small, low-risk project of ~21 thin prompt-only Agent subclasses plus two logic-bearing files (OrchestratorAgent static helpers, AgentRegistration); no correctness bugs found, but a startup race on the registration flag and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling are worth noting.
- **Birko.AI.Contracts** (7): Small, mostly-clean contracts/POCO project; the main issues are AgentOptions.Clone/Merge silently dropping the OnLlmResponseReceived callback and a Dictionary round-trip that loses several fields, plus the LLM provider async surface taking no CancellationToken.
- **Birko.AI.Orchestration** (2): A small, mostly-clean orchestration project (POCO models + a dispatcher + a dependency analyzer); the only real defect is an inverted topological-sort result, plus a total absence of tests for the logic-bearing analyzer.
- **Birko.AI.Providers** (9): A functional 16-provider LLM adapter library with solid shared OpenAI/SSE helpers, but it carries two real URL-construction bugs that break several providers at runtime, an undisposed-HttpResponseMessage leak across every provider, and a complete absence of any test project.
- **Birko.AI.Resilience** (7): Small, mostly-sound resilience library with one real correctness bug (cost tracking can never match per-model pricing), a few logic/robustness weaknesses in rate limiting and state persistence, and a complete absence of a test project.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs** (6): The core background-jobs library is small, well-structured, and well-tested; findings are minor correctness/robustness edges and dead code rather than serious bugs.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.CosmosDB** (6): Small, well-structured backend that follows the store conventions (SetSettings, *Core delegation via the store, CancellationToken plumbed everywhere), but its FailAsync/PurgeAsync diverge from the IJobQueue contract and the sibling backends in ways that mis-classify exhausted jobs and ignore retry backoff.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.ElasticSearch** (4): Small, faithful clone of the tested SQL/MongoDB job-queue backends — no critical correctness bugs, but it carries a non-atomic dequeue claim (worse under ES near-real-time refresh), a dead IndexName constant, an inaccurate doc comment, and zero test coverage.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.JSON** (4): Small, clean file-based job-queue backend that compiles without nullable warnings and correctly resolves the single-result ReadAsync overload; the only issues are a dropped RetryPolicy.MaxRetries fallback, an unguarded dequeue read-modify-write, and a complete absence of backend-specific tests.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.MongoDB** (3): Small, clean MongoDB job-queue backend that faithfully mirrors the SQL backend; no correctness bugs, but it inherits a non-atomic dequeue race (with a native MongoDB primitive available and unused), carries a dead/misleading CollectionName property, and has no test sibling.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.RavenDB** (4): A small, well-structured RavenDB job-queue backend that mirrors the reference InMemory/SQL implementations correctly; no compile or null-safety bugs, with the only notable gaps being a non-atomic dequeue race (common to all persistent backends), a minor retry-fallback divergence from the reference, and a missing .Tests project.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.Redis** (6): Two files, no tests; the queue logic is mostly sound but contains a critical scheduling bug where delayed/scheduled jobs are dequeued immediately, plus a GetByStatus ordering deviation, ignored CancellationTokens, and a complete absence of tests.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.SQL** (5): Functionally sound model/queue mapping with correct read/update logic, but the dequeue path is not atomic (a real distributed-safety bug for the project's stated multi-worker use case) and the optional lock provider has a connection leak plus a misleading success return on non-PostgreSQL backends; the queue and lock provider have no tests.
- **Birko.BackgroundJobs.XML** (3): Small, well-structured XML job-queue backend that compiles cleanly and faithfully mirrors the JSON reference; the only real gaps are a missing test project and a non-atomic dequeue (acknowledged single-process scope).
- **Birko.Caching** (5): Small, well-structured caching abstraction in good health; the main concerns are a cache-stampede race in the per-key lock lifecycle, inconsistent CancellationToken observance, and a couple of test gaps.
- **Birko.Caching.Hybrid** (5): Small, well-structured two-tier cache that is mostly correct, but it leaks SemaphoreSlim locks unboundedly in GetOrSetAsync and has a couple of edge-case async-exception/option-capping concerns plus notable test gaps.
- **Birko.Caching.Redis** (5): Single-file Redis-backed ICache implementation that is structurally sound but has a real expiration-cap logic bug, a dead/wasteful Redis round-trip, framework-wide CancellationToken non-observance, and no test project at all.
- **Birko.Communication** (5): A tiny, low-risk base project (just IPort + AbstractPort for byte-oriented hardware ports); the code itself is sound, but both README.md and CLAUDE.md document an entirely fictional API that does not exist in source.
- **Birko.Communication.Bluetooth** (14): A small, mostly-skeletal BLE port adapter (4 source files, no tests) with several real correctness bugs around buffer handling, finalizer/dispose semantics, and cancellation, plus a large amount of placeholder/no-op platform code and documentation that describes an API the code does not implement.
- **Birko.Communication.Camera** (5): Small, focused project (3 source files) that shells out to ffmpeg for JPEG snapshots; mostly clean and conformant, but the process-capture path has a real deadlock risk from an undrained stderr pipe plus an orphaned-process leak on cancellation.
- **Birko.Communication.GraphQL** (7): Small, well-structured client; core query/mutation path is correct, but the WebSocket subscription path has a real protocol-version mismatch and frame-handling bugs, and a request-level lock needlessly serializes all traffic through a shared client.
- **Birko.Communication.gRPC** (5): A small, well-structured client wrapper project that is largely clean; the main issues are unwired settings (DeadlineSeconds/ExtraMetadata), a doc-vs-code mismatch on credential inference, and a header-accumulation risk when CallOptions metadata is reused across calls.
- **Birko.Communication.gRPC.Server** (2): Small, clean three-file project (settings, DI extension, server auth interceptor) with no correctness bugs; only minor test-coverage gaps on the three streaming interceptor handler kinds.
- **Birko.Communication.Hardware** (9): Small port-communication library (3 source files) with several real correctness bugs: an LPT store that writes to the wrong I/O address and throws on RemoveReadData, an undisposed SerialPort resource leak, a latent null-deref when settings is null, and a thread-safety gap around the shared ReadData buffer; it also has zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Communication.IR** (5): Mostly clean, well-structured IR library; the one real defect is that RC5 encode emits a leading zero-duration mark that its own decoder rejects, so RC5 cannot round-trip — and there is no test covering it.
- **Birko.Communication.Modbus** (6): A small, focused, generally-correct Modbus master implementation with good test coverage; the main real-world risk is a partial-frame read on slow/streaming transports (RTU serial) and a missing transaction-ID validation, both of which the in-memory test mock cannot surface.
- **Birko.Communication.Network** (6): Two small AbstractPort implementations (TcpIp, Udp) that are functional for the happy path but carry several real concurrency bugs around the shared ReadData buffer, a negative-size crash in RemoveReadData, and have zero test coverage (no .Tests sibling exists).
- **Birko.Communication.NFC** (8): A small, generally well-structured NFC communication library with sound NDEF/ISO14443A parsing and bounds checks; the main risks are an undisposed transport resource leak in NfcReaderPort, a null-deref race in the HID transport's cancellation callback, and missing tests for the port and the serial/HTTP transports.
- **Birko.Communication.OAuth** (4): Small, well-structured OAuth2 client library that is largely correct and null-safe; the one real bug is the 401-retry path in OAuthDelegatingHandler resending an already-sent HttpRequestMessage, plus a redundant refresh attempt and a couple of test gaps that give false confidence.
- **Birko.Communication.OAuth.Providers** (2): Tiny single-file static factory for GitHub device-flow OAuth clients; correct and convention-clean, with one minor duplication and a missing test project.
- **Birko.Communication.REST** (7): A single thin HttpClient-wrapping RestClient; functionally mostly sound but has a real thread-safety bug in the static client cache, a non-functional Credentials property, and a CLAUDE.md that bears almost no resemblance to the actual code.
- **Birko.Communication.REST.Server** (6): Small, self-contained HttpListener-based REST host plus auth middleware; functionally sound but has a JSON-injection bug in the RestResponse error factories, a few correctness/cleanup issues, a missing IDisposable declaration, and a complete absence of test coverage for the Server project.
- **Birko.Communication.SOAP** (9): A small, mostly clean SOAP client/server pair with one significant correctness bug (credentials are silently never applied to outgoing requests), a thread-unsafe client cache, a deadlock-prone sync-over-async Dispose, and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Communication.SSE** (11): A small, mostly-scaffold SSE client/server + middleware library whose core network paths are unimplemented stubs; it has a handful of real correctness bugs (custom SemaphoreSlim leak, dropped reason text, query-string parsing edge cases, double-connect CTS leak) and zero test coverage (no .Tests sibling exists).
- **Birko.Communication.WebSocket** (7): Small ASP.NET Core / client WebSocket project that is mostly sound, but has a handful of real correctness bugs around sync-over-async blocking, listener lifecycle, and a negative-size RemoveRange crash, plus thin test coverage.
- **Birko.Configuration** (5): Small, single-file settings hierarchy that is mostly sound, but the LoadFrom overrides in PasswordSettings/RemoteSettings silently break the base copy contract for less-derived inputs, and there are no tests at all.
- **Birko.Contracts** (4): A small, clean zero-dependency contracts project; the only behavioral logic (RetryPolicy.GetDelay) has an overflow edge case that can yield a negative delay, and the project has no test sibling.
- **Birko.CQRS** (5): A small, clean MediatR-style CQRS library that is well-tested for the happy path, but the mediator's handler cache has a latent correctness bug when the same request type is dispatched with different TResult type arguments (e.g. via IRequest covariance).
- **Birko.Data.Aggregates** (3): A small, well-structured aggregate flatten/expand mapping library with good test coverage; correctness is mostly sound but two real latent issues exist around type-casting of resolved related data and the handling of unsaved (null-Guid) child entities during expand.
- **Birko.Data.Composition** (1): A small, well-designed single-file utility (StoreWrapperBuilder) that is correct and convention-compliant; its only gap is the complete absence of test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.Core** (4): Small, low-risk contracts/models project that is largely clean; the main concern is a CopyTo pattern that can return null behind a suppressing ! operator, plus a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.CosmosDB** (8): Functionally structured and convention-aware, but contains one fundamental document-id/partition-key correctness bug and three lazy-init-breaking convention violations (public CRUD overridden instead of *Core) that would surface in real usage.
- **Birko.Data.CosmosDB.ViewModel** (3): A small, clean two-file ViewModel-repository wrapper that faithfully mirrors the known-good MongoDB sibling; the only real issue is a redundant store-destroy in the async repository.
- **Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Views** (6): A small, generally well-structured view store, but the aggregate query path has two real correctness bugs (ORDER BY and WHERE reference view-property names against raw documents that carry source-property names), plus a few SQL-injection / type-handling gaps in the hand-rolled filter translator, and the project ships with zero tests.
- **Birko.Data.ElasticSearch** (7): Solid, well-structured ElasticSearch backend; the main issues are a public CRUD override that bypasses lazy-init and silently caps results, plus dead/broken helper code and large test gaps on the highest-risk store paths.
- **Birko.Data.ElasticSearch.ViewModel** (4): Tiny, healthy project (two abstract base repositories closely mirroring the Birko.Data.ElasticSearch reference); the only real issue is a wrapped-store handling inconsistency in the sync Count/ClearCache helpers, plus async-surface asymmetry and a total absence of tests.
- **Birko.Data.ElasticSearch.Views** (5): Small, well-structured 2-file view adapter that is largely correct, but it silently returns the full dataset when a filter expression can't be translated, has a Manager/Store index-name resolution mismatch, and ships with zero tests.
- **Birko.Data.EventSourcing** (5): A small, well-structured decorator library that is functionally broken for the common "create with no pre-assigned Guid" path — the recorded event's AggregateId never matches the entity's persisted Guid, defeating Replay/GetHistory — and ships with a README describing an API that does not exist and no test project.
- **Birko.Data.InfluxDB** (7): Functional store/repository implementation that follows the *Core override convention correctly, but has a real IDisposable client leak, an inconsistent SaveAsync path that bypasses lazy-init and retry, and thin test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.InfluxDB.ViewModel** (4): Tiny project (2 thin repository wrappers) that is essentially a copy of Birko.Data.InfluxDB's repositories; it is functionally sound but carries a redundant double-destroy of the store, dead usings, and has zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.InMemory** (2): Small, well-structured store backend that correctly follows framework conventions (overrides *Core methods, guard clauses, snapshot materialization, no nullable warnings); only trivial cleanup observations, no correctness bugs.
- **Birko.Data.JSON** (10): A functional file-based store family, but the synchronous Separate/Batch/single-file stores contain several correctness bugs (a save/load shape mismatch, guaranteed KeyNotFoundException on create, and an inverted Destroy guard) that are masked because the .Tests sibling only exercises JsonStore's no-op paths and never round-trips data through the sync separate/batch variants.
- **Birko.Data.JSON.ViewModel** (2): Clean, minimal project: two thin ViewModel repository wrappers that faithfully follow the same store-validation pattern used across all sibling .ViewModel projects; no correctness bugs found, only trivial cleanup and a missing test sibling.
- **Birko.Data.Localization** (9): A well-structured entity-localization decorator layer that is mostly correct; the main issues are an inconsistent default-culture guard in the bulk wrappers, dead/incomplete OrderBy-splitting code, and a few lazy-enumeration / native-update edge cases.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations** (3): A small, clean abstraction-only project (interfaces, base classes, result/exception types) with no concrete stores or settings; the main concerns are a sync-over-async async surface and absent cancellation support, plus no dedicated core tests project.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.CosmosDB** (7): Functionally reasonable Cosmos migration backend that faithfully mirrors the other migration backends, but it has a correctness bug in the runner's failed-migration index calculation, a likely-wrong partition-key assumption in the schema builder, a destructive RenameField implementation, and zero test coverage (no .Tests sibling exists).
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.ElasticSearch** (8): Functional and conventionally aligned with the other Migrations backends, but the data migrator has a real Painless-script injection/formatting bug, the migrations store can miscount versions due to a hardcoded search cap plus a missing post-write refresh, several declared settings are dead, and there is no .Tests sibling at all.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.InfluxDB** (9): Functionally reasonable for a schema-less time-series migration backend, but has a resource leak (undisposed batching WriteApi), several sync-over-async blocking calls, ignored CancellationToken, and zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.MongoDB** (6): Functional for basic record-keeping and data ops, but the transaction handling is broken (session never joins operations), index creation is a silent no-op, and the failure path can throw a masking out-of-range exception; the project also has no test sibling.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.RavenDB** (9): Small provider (6 files) whose state store and runner are sound, but the data-migrator and schema-builder contain several outright-broken methods (CountDocuments, CopyData, CollectionExists, BulkInsert), a missing System.Linq import that breaks compilation under the project's explicit-using convention, and there is no .Tests sibling at all.
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.SQL** (8): The production code has one serious correctness bug (schema-builder CREATE TABLE/INDEX never executes) and a transactional-consistency bug in migration recording; separately the .Tests project does not compile at all (missing imports + references a non-existent SqlMigration API).
- **Birko.Data.Migrations.TimescaleDB** (4): Small, focused project that correctly extends the SQL migration infrastructure, but has three concrete correctness bugs (a dropped connector, hardcoded compression columns, and a malformed GROUP BY) plus a complete absence of tests.
- **Birko.Data.MongoDB** (7): Functionally solid and broadly idiomatic, but several public CRUD overrides bypass the framework's lazy-init/cancellation gate, a change-stream DocumentKey bug never populates the GUID for String-represented models, and store/settings/index-manager/UoW code has no tests.
- **Birko.Data.MongoDB.ViewModel** (3): Two thin ViewModel-repository wrappers (sync + async) that faithfully mirror the sibling Birko.Data.MongoDB repository pattern; correct overall, with only redundant double-destroy logic and a complete absence of a test sibling.
- **Birko.Data.MongoDB.Views** (5): Small, mostly-clean MongoDB view translator/store/manager trio, but it has one real correctness bug (the base aggregation pipeline is re-applied on top of an already-projected persistent MongoDB view), a likely-dead Auto-mode fallback path, an invalid SharedGUID, and no .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.Patterns** (7): A small, well-structured patterns library (decorators, specifications, paging, concurrency) that is mostly clean, but has a real interface-dispatch bug in RuleSpecification, a parallel-store-access bug in the async slug bulk wrapper, several multiple-enumeration hazards, and a complete absence of a test project covering all the wrapper logic.
- **Birko.Data.Processors** (8): A small, well-structured streaming-processor library (CSV/XML formats + HTTP/ZIP transport decorators) that is mostly solid, but the ZIP extraction path has a Zip-Slip vulnerability and breaks on archives with nested folders, and the async CSV/XML paths have real async-correctness rough edges.
- **Birko.Data.RavenDB** (5): Generally solid store backend that follows the *Core override pattern in most places, but the single-item/parameterless Read overrides bypass lazy-init (a real correctness bug + convention violation), and async bulk insert plus single-Read ignore the CancellationToken.
- **Birko.Data.RavenDB.ViewModel** (3): Tiny, clean two-file project (sync + async RavenDB ViewModel repositories) that correctly follows framework conventions; no correctness bugs found, the only material gap is the complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.RavenDB.Views** (5): Small, mostly-correct view backend (3 source files); the main risk is an Avg aggregate that produces wrong results under RavenDB's incremental re-reduce, plus a complete absence of tests for all public functionality.
- **Birko.Data.Repositories** (5): Thin, well-documented wrapper layer over Birko.Data.Stores that is structurally sound, but has one real double-destroy bug, genuine thread-safety races in RepositoryLocator (which advertises itself as thread-safe), and zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.SQL** (8): Mature, well-factored SQL store layer with correct *Core override conventions and strong expression-parsing coverage; a few real async correctness bugs (lock released before async work completes, CancellationToken not threaded through reader execution) and swallowed-exception control flow warrant fixes.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.Caching** (5): A small, mostly correct caching subclass of AsyncDataBaseBulkStore, but it has a real cache-coherency bug (filter-based bulk writes bypass invalidation) and its README documents a different (decorator) API than what is actually implemented, plus there is no .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.MSSql** (8): Bulk operations and settings chain are mostly sound, but the type-conversion table has several data-loss mappings and the sync store's RemoteSettings handling silently breaks connections, and there is no .Tests sibling at all.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.MSSql.View** (7): A small SQL Server view-DDL extension that is mostly correct, but its indexed-view methods skip the view-existence cache invalidation the base class performs, lean on sync-over-async wrappers instead of the framework's async connector primitives, duplicate ~140 lines of the base view-select builder, and have no test coverage at all.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.MySQL** (4): A small, well-structured MySQL store/connector that faithfully mirrors the MSSQL/PostgreSQL dialect siblings; the main gap is a complete absence of a .Tests sibling, plus a few minor cleanups.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.MySQL.View** (2): A single-file partial-class provider override (MySQL ViewExists via information_schema) that is correct, parameterized, properly disposes its reader, and faithfully mirrors the sibling MSSql/PostgreSQL implementations; the only notes are a missing async override and the absence of a test project.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.PostgreSQL** (5): Small, well-structured PostgreSQL store/connector that closely mirrors the MSSql sibling and follows the framework's *Core override and Settings-chain conventions; no critical bugs, but there is a complete absence of a .Tests sibling and a few minor cleanups.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.PostgreSQL.View** (2): A small, single-file partial connector adding PostgreSQL materialized-view DDL; it is largely correct and consistent with the sibling MSSql.View, with no correctness bugs but a complete absence of tests for its public surface.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite** (5): Functional store/connector layer with a correctly-structured *Core override pattern, but the native bulk operations silently swallow failures and skip the framework's transient-retry path, and the SQLite index manager's ListAsync override is unreachable through the interface/base, so GetInfoAsync returns wrong data.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.SqLite.View** (3): A tiny, well-formed two-method connector partial that correctly overrides the sync view DDL primitives; the only substantive issue is that the SQLite-specific existence logic is absent on the async path, plus there is no test sibling.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.View** (8): Functionally coherent SQL view layer (attribute-driven on-the-fly + persistent view querying), but carries one real concurrency bug in the static view cache, a constructor that discards its name argument, several null-deref/NRE risks reachable through public APIs, and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.View.Migrations** (3): Small, well-guarded integration project (2 static classes); no correctness bugs found, but it duplicates ~140 lines of view-SQL generation from AbstractConnectorBase and the entire ViewMigrationExtensions execution surface is untested.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.ViewModel** (4): Small project (4 source files, ~180 LOC); the sync repository is internally consistent, but the async repository has a generic-invariance type bug that makes it effectively unusable with any real concrete store, and the project has no test sibling at all.
- **Birko.Data.SQL.Views** (5): A small, mostly-correct SQL translator + view store/manager, but the async surface is entirely sync-over-async (blocks on synchronous connector calls despite available *Async connector methods), the GroupBy clause is silently dropped, and the project ships with zero tests.
- **Birko.Data.Stores** (5): Small, well-structured abstraction layer that is largely clean and convention-compliant; the only correctness concern is an unintended mutation of caller data in the LINQ aggregation time-bucket path, plus minor async-consistency and dead-code cleanups.
- **Birko.Data.Sync** (10): A reflection-based two-store synchronization provider that is structurally sound but carries several correctness bugs in change-tracking persistence, NewestWins timestamp detection, and cancellation/error result reporting, plus unreachable conflict logic and unused option fields.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.CosmosDB** (6): Small, mostly-correct store pair that cleanly extends the CosmosDB base, but it carries a multi-tenant correctness bug (tenantId is accepted everywhere and never applied), some unguarded null derefs around item.Guid, and has zero tests.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.ElasticSearch** (3): Small project (2 source files) that correctly mirrors the MongoDB sync sibling, but the ElasticSearch model maps a property onto the reserved _id metadata field and carries two unused fields; there are no tests.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.Json** (4): A small, mostly-clean 2-file store backend that correctly extends AsyncJsonStore and follows the *Core-override and bulk-Read conventions; the only material issues are an O(N) file-rewrite pattern in SetLastSyncTimeAsync, a complete absence of tests, and a vestigial Id field.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.MongoDb** (3): Small, healthy 2-file shared project that faithfully mirrors the verified JSON/ElasticSearch sync siblings; no correctness bugs, but it has a misleading dead CollectionName property, an unused field, and no test project at all.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.RavenDB** (8): Small 3-file project whose store logic compiles but is functionally broken in several places: the tenant filter never matches, the async delete uses the wrong RavenDB overload, and the upsert path creates duplicate documents because the stable document-id helper is never wired in; it also has no test project.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.Sql** (3): A small, clean SQL sync-knowledge backend (3 files, ~200 LOC) that faithfully mirrors the JSON reference store and follows framework store conventions; no correctness bugs, but it ships with zero dedicated tests and has a minor no-op-upsert edge in SetLastSyncTime inherited from the reference implementation.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.Tenant** (10): A small tenant-aware sync layer that is mostly sound, but the core sync engine in TenantSyncProvider has several correctness bugs around knowledge-item bookkeeping, non-deterministic version hashing, swallowed exceptions, and shared-state mutation, plus no .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.Sync.Xml** (2): Small, clean two-file project that faithfully mirrors the SQL/JSON sync-store reference implementations; no correctness bugs found, the only real gap is missing test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.Tagging** (5): Small, clean abstract tagging library (3 models, 1 service base, 1 DI extension); no correctness bugs of note, but it ships with zero tests and has a couple of efficiency/redundancy cleanups plus a convention nit in the projitems GUID.
- **Birko.Data.Tenant** (7): Small, well-structured multi-tenancy library (tenant context, store wrappers, filter, ASP.NET middleware, DI helpers) that is functionally sound; the notable gaps are a complete absence of tests, a couple of robustness issues in bulk wrappers and async Save, and a static-singleton-vs-DI footgun.
- **Birko.Data.TimescaleDB** (5): Small, well-structured store backend that correctly follows the *Core override convention and observes cancellation; the main concern is that the custom TimescaleDBSettings.GetConnectionString() is never used by the connector, so configured timeouts/SSL are silently dropped, and test coverage is near-zero.
- **Birko.Data.TimescaleDB.ViewModel** (4): A tiny (2-file, ~180 LOC) repository project that faithfully mirrors the already-reviewed Birko.Data.TimescaleDB repositories; no correctness bugs, but it ships with zero tests and carries a couple of minor robustness/clarity nits inherited from the sibling pattern.
- **Birko.Data.ViewModel** (7): Small abstractions-only project (8 repository interface/abstract files); the interface layer is clean, but the bulk abstract implementations have a real correctness bug (transform-delegate return values discarded), inconsistent change-tracking between sync and async bulk paths, dead null-filtering, a stale README documenting non-existent ViewModel classes, and no .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Data.Views** (4): A small, clean definition/builder/interface library (no concrete store implementations) with thorough tests; only minor robustness and validation-consistency observations, no correctness bugs.
- **Birko.Data.XML** (9): Functionally correct for the single-file XmlStore/AsyncXmlStore, but the Separate and Batch store variants have serious persistence bugs (bulk writes silently don't persist, batch stores never batch, and a write/read serialization mismatch loses data on reload), compounded by near-absent test coverage.
- **Birko.Data.XML.ViewModel** (2): Clean — two thin abstract ViewModel repository wrappers that faithfully mirror the canonical JSON.ViewModel sibling and the framework conventions; no correctness bugs found.
- **Birko.EventBus** (8): Small, well-structured in-process event bus that is largely clean; the main issues are ErrorHandlingMode.Stop not being honored in parallel dispatch, silently swallowed handler exceptions despite a "Log and continue" contract, and a deduplication mark/check race.
- **Birko.EventBus.EventSourcing** (3): Small, clean bridge layer (3 files, ~150 LOC) with correct async/cancellation handling and good test coverage; only minor issues around the DomainEventPublished wrapper dropping original event identity/timestamp and a missing null guard.
- **Birko.EventBus.MessageQueue** (6): Small, well-structured distributed event bus over IMessageQueue; largely correct, but two functional gaps around error handling/retry and several configured options that are never consumed.
- **Birko.EventBus.Outbox** (6): A small, clean transactional-outbox library that is structurally sound, but has two genuine correctness gaps (the MaxAttempts option is never enforced, and the Publishing/claim status is never used so concurrent or overlapping processors can double-publish) plus a diagnostic bug from reflection exception wrapping; no .Tests sibling exists at all.
- **Birko.Health** (3): A small, clean, well-tested standalone health-check library with no correctness bugs; only a couple of low-severity hardening/test-gap observations.
- **Birko.Health.Azure** (3): A small, clean two-file health-check project that correctly follows the established Birko.Health pattern; the only substantive issue is that both checks swallow OperationCanceledException, which defeats the HealthCheckRunner's timeout-status handling.
- **Birko.Health.Data** (5): A small, focused, low-risk health-check library that is largely sound; the main recurring issue is an undisposed internally-created HttpClient across the six HTTP-based checks, plus a couple of missing-timeout and test-coverage gaps.
- **Birko.Health.Redis** (3): Small, single-file health-check project that faithfully mirrors the reference DiskSpaceHealthCheck pattern and is essentially correct; the only material gap is a missing test sibling, plus a couple of minor robustness/cancellation notes.
- **Birko.Helpers** (5): Small, mostly clean utility library; the main concern is that PathValidator's path-containment checks use a naive StartsWith that the project's own PathHelper.IsUnderDirectory already demonstrates is unsafe (sibling-prefix escape), plus a couple of edge-case gaps and test coverage holes.
- **Birko.Localization** (6): A small, cleanly-structured localization library that is largely correct; the most significant issue is FormatCurrency ignoring its currencyCode parameter, plus a couple of minor robustness/cleanup items.
- **Birko.Localization.Data** (4): Small, clean, well-tested project (one translation provider over an injected async bulk read store) with no real correctness bugs; the only notable item is the synchronous interface forcing a sync-over-async blocking pattern.
- **Birko.MessageQueue (core)** (4): The core project is almost entirely interfaces and POCOs with sound contracts; the only non-trivial logic lives in RetryPolicy.GetDelay (which has an integer-overflow edge) and that logic plus DeadLetterOptions have no test coverage.
- **Birko.MessageQueue.InMemory** (9): Small, well-structured Channels-based in-memory queue that mostly works, but it has a resource leak (the channel and its per-destination CancellationTokenSources / dispatch loops are never disposed), an unobserved fire-and-forget delayed-send, a no-op requeue path, and a dead options class.
- **Birko.MessageQueue.MQTT** (8): A small, generally well-structured MQTTnet wrapper with one genuine concurrency race and a typed-message data-loss issue; no test project exists at all.
- **Birko.MessageQueue.Redis** (8): Functional Redis Streams queue with a clean producer/consumer split, but the consumer's redelivery/reject path and CancellationToken handling have real correctness gaps, and the background poll loop can die silently.
- **Birko.Messaging** (4): Small, clean messaging project (Email/SMS/Push DTOs + SMTP sender + template engine); the only real correctness concern is sharing a non-thread-safe SmtpClient, plus a couple of minor robustness/test-gap notes.
- **Birko.Messaging.Razor** (6): Small, focused 3-file Razor template engine that is mostly well-structured, but has one inverted caching condition, a weakened directory-traversal check, pervasive non-observance of CancellationToken, and no test project despite CLAUDE.md requiring one.
- **Birko.Models** (5): Small, mostly clean model/value-object project; no correctness-critical bugs, but it has zero test coverage and a few LoadFrom/CopyTo inconsistencies worth tightening.
- **Birko.Models.Category** (4): A tiny, dependency-light pure-model project (4 source files, no stores/async) that is largely clean; the main issues are LoadFrom round-trip data loss for hierarchy fields and the complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Contracts** (4): A tiny, mostly-clean contracts project; the only real risks are concentrated in HierarchyHelper — a documented "zero-dependency" violation and several unguarded Path null-dereferences.
- **Birko.Models.Customers** (5): A small, pure model/viewmodel/filter project (no stores or async) that is mostly clean, but has two real correctness gaps in the Model layer's CopyTo/LoadFrom plumbing and a complete absence of a test sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Customers.SQL** (4): Tiny, purely-declarative IModelMapping project that is correct as far as it goes, but its mappings are inconsistent — three of four entities map only the primary key while sibling domains map every string column with explicit precision — and it ships with no test sibling and no .gitignore.
- **Birko.Models.Inventory** (4): A small, clean POCO model/viewmodel domain project with no stores, async, or disposable resources; the only real issues are model-to-viewmodel mapping gaps (a contract field and the document lines never round-trip) plus a fully absent .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Inventory.SQL** (2): A small, clean declarative SQL-mapping project (3 IModelMapping classes); no correctness bugs, no convention violations, only a missing test sibling and one harmless redundant call.
- **Birko.Models.Pricing** (3): A clean, small POCO-only domain project (models, view models, filters) with no correctness bugs, but it ships with zero tests and a couple of minor mapping/consistency gaps.
- **Birko.Models.Pricing.SQL** (1): Clean, minimal declarative SQL-mapping project: a single correct mapping file fully consistent with sibling domain conventions; the only gap is the absence of a test sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Product** (4): A small, mostly-clean POCO model/viewmodel/filter project; the only real correctness risk is a broken LINQ-expression composition in ProductList.Filter(), plus a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Product.SQL** (2): Clean, minimal project — two declarative IModelMapping files matching the established sibling pattern exactly, with no correctness, nullability, async, or disposal concerns; only minor consistency and test-coverage observations.
- **Birko.Models.SEO** (4): A tiny, low-risk model-only project (Model + ViewModel + 2 filters, no stores/async/settings) that is broadly clean; the only real concerns are a latent null-deref in the path filter, one inconsistent property setter, and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Models.SQL** (3): A small, dependency-light fluent SQL-mapping framework (4 files, no stores/async/IDisposable) that is structurally sound, with one meaningful behavioral gap (configured field metadata silently dropped on apply), some avoidable reflection, and a complete absence of a test sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Users** (4): A clean, small POCO/ViewModel/Filter domain project (no stores/async/settings/IDisposable, so the heavy-risk categories don't apply); the only real correctness concern is an unguarded `data.Guid!.Value` dereference in the relational models' LoadFrom overloads, plus a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Models.Users.SQL** (3): Small, pure declarative SQL-mapping library (8 IModelMapping configs, no runtime logic) — correctness-clean with no bugs, nullable, or async concerns; the only gaps are missing FK uniqueness/index constraints on relationship tables and a total absence of a tests sibling.
- **Birko.Random** (6): Small, well-structured standalone RNG library (providers, distributions, sequences, noise) that is mostly clean; the one real correctness bug is a unit mismatch in SnowflakeGenerator's millisecond-rollover path.
- **Birko.Redis** (5): Small (2-file) infrastructure project that is largely correct and convention-compliant; the only real concerns are a Lazy-connection exception-caching footgun, a fragile GetServer endpoint-parse, and the complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Rules** (4): A small, well-structured, dependency-free rule engine that is largely clean; the main issues are a semantic inconsistency for disabled rules inside groups and an unsynchronized static property cache.
- **Birko.Security** (5): A small, well-written security primitives library (password hashing, AES-GCM encryption, token/secret abstractions, token-binding auth) that is correct on the crypto core but has a real disposal/leak bug, a couple of missing input guards that turn bad input into exceptions instead of clean failures, and zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Security.AspNetCore** (4): Small, mostly clean ASP.NET Core security integration, but it carries one real correctness bug: tokens minted by TokenServiceAdapter pack multi-value role/permission claims with a separator that the runtime ClaimsCurrentUser reader never splits on, so permission/role checks silently fail on the live JWT path.
- **Birko.Security.AzureKeyVault** (5): Small, well-structured single-provider project that is largely correct; the main issue is mutating a caller-injected HttpClient's Timeout, plus a few minor cleanups and test gaps.
- **Birko.Security.BCrypt** (4): A single-file, hand-rolled BCrypt/Blowfish implementation whose key-expansion deviates from the canonical EksBlowfish spec, so its "$2a$"-labelled output is almost certainly not interoperable with real BCrypt — and no known-answer test exists to detect it.
- **Birko.Security.Jwt** (4): A small, well-structured single-class JWT provider that is largely correct; the main gaps are an unguarded null parameter in GenerateToken and a complete absence of any test project.
- **Birko.Security.NFC** (4): Small, well-structured NFC auth provider that is largely clean — no correctness bugs, proper async/await with CancellationToken observed throughout, no resource leaks; the few findings are minor robustness, a dead result property, and a token-issuance test gap.
- **Birko.Security.OAuth.Server** (5): A well-structured, RFC-faithful OAuth2 authorization server with no correctness bugs found; the main opportunities are de-duplicating the copy-pasted NarrowScope helper and a couple of security-hardening gaps (no token-family revocation on refresh/code reuse) plus minor test-coverage notes.
- **Birko.Security.Vault** (5): Small, focused HTTP-API Vault secret provider that is largely sound, with one clear correctness bug (UpdatedAt populated from created_time), a couple of robustness/null-safety gaps in JSON parsing, and notable test gaps for the write/delete/pairs paths.
- **Birko.Security.Vault.Configuration** (3): Small, well-structured configuration-integration project that is functionally sound; the only material gaps are inconsistent argument-null guarding in two extension overloads and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Serialization** (3): A small, clean serialization abstraction (ISerializer + System.Text.Json and System.Xml.Serialization implementations) that is well-guarded and correct overall, with a few cancellation-token and XML-encoding edge issues plus a sizeable test gap on the stream/async overloads.
- **Birko.Serialization.MessagePack** (3): A single small, correct ISerializer implementation over MessagePack; no bugs or convention violations, only minor needless allocations on the stream paths and some untested stream/async surface.
- **Birko.Serialization.Newtonsoft** (2): A single small, well-structured ISerializer implementation with correct null-guarding and disposal; no correctness bugs, only a minor cancellation-observance nit and a test-coverage gap on the stream/async overloads.
- **Birko.Serialization.Protobuf** (3): A single-file, faithful ISerializer implementation that is largely correct and well-tested; the only real issues are async-method conventions (SerializeAsync ignores the CancellationToken, DeserializeAsync uses sync-over-async Task.Run) plus a couple of untested public surfaces.
- **Birko.Serialization.Yaml** (2): A single small, well-implemented ISerializer over YamlDotNet with correct null guards, stream lifetime handling, and UTF-8 encoding; no correctness bugs found, only a minor cancellation-observation gap and a couple of untested overloads.
- **Birko.Storage** (7): Small, well-structured file-storage abstraction with good local-storage test coverage; the main concerns are async methods that ignore the CancellationToken, a partial-file-on-failure leak in UploadAsync, and a prefix-collision weakness in the path-traversal guard.
- **Birko.Storage.AzureBlob** (8): Functionally solid REST-based Azure Blob storage adapter; one real resource leak in DownloadAsync and a SAS/URL encoding correctness gap are the notable issues, plus a few minor cleanups and a couple of weak tests.
- **Birko.Structures** (6): A clean, self-contained classic-data-structures library (graphs, heaps, tries, caches, trees, etc.) that builds without warnings; one genuine correctness bug in CompressedTrie prefix queries, plus a couple of minor shadowing/cleanup items and some untested public surface.
- **Birko.Telemetry** (5): Small, well-structured instrumentation library that is largely clean; the main substantive issue is that the bulk store wrappers do not forward ReadFirst/ReadFirstAsync, bypassing any native single-row optimization on the inner store, plus several test gaps.
- **Birko.Telemetry.OpenTelemetry** (3): A small, well-structured DI-extension wrapper (2 files, ~160 LOC) around the OpenTelemetry SDK; no correctness bugs found, with one design/documentation inconsistency around ASP.NET Core instrumentation defaulting on while its package is documented as optional.
- **Birko.Time** (5): Small, well-structured time/calendar library that is largely clean; the only notable issue is three dead duplicate source files shadowing the Abstractions sibling, plus a couple of minor validation/robustness gaps.
- **Birko.Time.Abstractions** (0): Clean, correct, and fully tested: a tiny zero-dependency clock abstraction (one interface, two implementations) with no bugs, convention violations, or test gaps.
- **Birko.Validation** (4): Small, well-structured validation library that is largely clean and correct; only a minor resource-leak and a couple of test-coverage gaps are worth noting.
- **Birko.Web.Components** (9): A large (~18k LOC), generally well-structured Shadow-DOM component library with good lifecycle hygiene in most components, but it has a few genuine correctness bugs (broken ordered-list markdown rendering, unescaped attribute interpolation in b-form, a leaked document listener and an off-by-one event index), and notably ships with zero automated tests.
- **Birko.Web.Core** (7): A small (~2k LOC) TypeScript front-end core library that is mostly solid, but carries a few real correctness bugs in its network/sync layers (WebSocket backoff reset, SyncManager state leak, i18n locale-restore gap) and a leaked consumer-specific constant, plus zero test coverage.
- **Birko.Web.Shell** (7): A well-structured TypeScript shell/UI library (no .cs code); core logic is sound, but it has a couple of unguarded-parse robustness bugs, some loading-state leaks on async failure, duplicated event wiring, and zero test coverage for its many pure helpers.
- **Birko.Workflow** (6): A small, well-structured in-memory workflow engine with good test breadth; no critical bugs, but a few state-consistency, design-contract, and minor correctness/test-gap items worth tightening.
- **Birko.Workflow.CosmosDB** (2): A small, healthy workflow-persistence wrapper that closely mirrors the RavenDB reference backend; one minor behavioral divergence and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling are the only notable issues.
- **Birko.Workflow.ElasticSearch** (4): Small, well-structured ElasticSearch workflow-persistence backend that compiles cleanly and matches its sibling backends; the only material issues are a couple of unguarded JSON-deserialization paths and a complete absence of a .Tests sibling.
- **Birko.Workflow.JSON** (3): Small, clean wrapper around AsyncJsonStore for workflow-instance persistence; it compiles without errors and follows store conventions, with the only real gaps being a nullable-suppression on deserialized data and a complete absence of tests.
- **Birko.Workflow.MongoDB** (4): Small, correct backend that faithfully mirrors the Birko.Workflow.JSON reference; no correctness bugs, but it carries a dead/misleading collection-name property, a null-masking suppression, an effectively no-op schema helper, and has no test sibling.
- **Birko.Workflow.RavenDB** (4): Small (3-file), clean RavenDB workflow-instance persistence backend that builds with zero errors and no nullable warnings; the only issues are a missing test project and a fragile reliance on single-result ReadAsync overload binding instead of the framework's recommended ReadFirstAsync.
- **Birko.Workflow.SQL** (4): Small, idiomatic SQL workflow-persistence backend that faithfully mirrors the Birko.Workflow.JSON reference implementation; it compiles cleanly with no nullable warnings and has no correctness bugs, but carries a couple of low/medium-severity robustness and test-coverage gaps.
- **Birko.Workflow.XML** (2): Small, well-structured XML workflow-persistence backend that faithfully mirrors the JSON sibling; one genuine correctness bug in a default field value, plus a missing dedicated test project.
